notes.title: 3. Isles of Abyss Permanent Server Opening Schedule

items.text: To meet everyone's long-term need to play on the Isles of Abyss, each region will open 1 Permanent Server on November 18, 2026 （PT）: Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server). Metas from the Isles of Abyss server will eventually all gather on this server.

Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server) will open a sufficient number of Basic Worlds and Vision Worlds to ensure a smooth experience for Metas. Vision Worlds will synchronize with the Visional Wheel "Dissonant Resonance" game mode. The official team will subsequently evaluate adding more worlds based on server operation conditions and Metas' gameplay needs; any adjustments will be explained through future announcements.

To ensure a smooth and stable experience for Metas participating in wilderness gameplay, territory construction, and resource gathering, certain mechanics within the same world currently have capacity limits. The relevant rules are as follows:

1) When the number of online players in a world reaches its cap, subsequent Metas will temporarily be unable to enter that world. You may switch to another world to play. If your territory is located in the world that has reached its player cap, you can still enter that world and will not be affected by this restriction.

2) Within the same world, certain game modes will also have a limit on how many can be active simultaneously. If the mode you want to play in your current world has reached its activation cap, you can switch to another world to experience it.
3) When the number of territories placed within the same world reaches the limit, no more territories can be placed. At that point, Metas will need to switch to another world to place territories.

notes.title: 3.2 How to Enter Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server)

items.text: 1) Automatic system merge (for characters already in the Isles of Abyss scenario)

After the Isles of Abyss server has been running for 31 days, players on the server will automatically be merged into Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server). After the merge, data such as Hives, backpack supplies, and territories will be retained according to the rules, and Metas can continue to play on the permanent server.
2) Enter via Server List (for new characters or signing up to enter)

Once the Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server) opens, it will appear in the server selection list. Metas can go to Scenario Selection - Isles of Abyss - More Server Options - Permanent Server, select Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server), and enter that server.

Note: The gameplay of Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server) runs by default according to the \[End of Storm\] phase rules of the Isles of Abyss scenario. The overall challenge intensity is relatively high. If you use a new character or sign up to enter, please familiarize yourself with the rules and difficulty of this phase in advance, and choose carefully based on your own situation.

notes.title: 3.3 Isles of Abyss (Permanent Server) Game Mode Description

items.text: The Isles of Abyss Permanent Server stays permanently in the \[End of Storm\] phase. The relevant gameplay rules are as follows:
1) The Sunken Lord: Can be unlocked directly without reaching the Purification Progress. Metas can go to the entrance and enter the challenge directly.
2) Calamity Tower: Calamity Tower - Abyss difficulty is unlocked directly and refreshes on a specific cycle. Each World can refresh at most 1 Calamity Tower - Abyss.

3) Scenario Challenge: After the system automatically merges you into the permanent server, your progress will be uniformly reset to the current new permanent server's scenario challenge tasks and rewards, ensuring a consistent experience for both new and veteran players after the merge.

notes.title: IV. Custom Server Adds New \[Dissonant Resonance\] Scenario Selection

items.text: As the Visional Wheel turns, Custom Server simultaneously adds new configurable scenarios: Manibus (Vision: Dissonant Resonance), Endless Dream (Vision: Gravity Abyss), The Way of Winter (Vision: Dissonant Resonance), Deviation: Survive, Capture, Preserve (Vision: Gravity Abyss), Prismverse's Clash (Vision: Dissonant Resonance), and Isles of Abyss (Vision: Dissonant Resonance). Metas can choose to experience others' servers in Custom Server, or open 1 Custom Server of their own to experience.

That's all for this announcement. For actual server opening times, please check in-game. If you have any questions or suggestions, feel free to reach out to us via the Feedback Platform （Once Human Feedback Platform).
Once Human Development Team

Hello. I came back to fix a few things.

You can now enable/disable the “Camera Smoothing” for gamepads in the Gameplay Settings. The setting is turned off by default, because a few people mentioned experiencing nausea due to the smoothing. The default behaviour should now feel familiar if you’re used to other games where the camera stops moving immediately when you release R-stick. If you liked the smoothing, you can turn it back on.

Fixed an issue with cloud save files not working across different systems when their system locales were different (e.g. playing on your French PC and loading that save on a Steam Deck). Save files are now consistent no matter which system or locale you are using. The game should also still be able to read legacy save files in case you previously saved using a certain locale.

Vulkan rendering should now work properly on Windows again (see Patch 1.783.1129 Notes). I’ve kept the launch options for now because DirectX12 should theoretically remain more stable on Windows, but Vulkan is back for the extra FPS if you want it.
If this update introduces any new issues for you, please let me know. And in the meantime you could always use the revert branch to go back to the previous version and finish your playthrough.
Cheers!
Lars (snekflat)

Version 1.2 of SiN Reloaded is now live, bringing several adjustments to levels, gameplay, multiplayer, and bug fixes.
Major Feature: Save Compatibility

This version introduces a new save compatibility system that retroactively applies to all old saves (both from the initial launch version and Patch 1.1). Players can load saves from these versions and continue to play the episode that they were playing from that version without losing any data. Once you transition to the next episode, however, you will then be playing on the latest levels.

The upside is you can continue to play your saved games, even after patching, without any issues. The downside, however, is that you may experience some minor bugs that were fixed in later versions if you load that episode from an old save. If you’re concerned about that, you can simply use the Episode Select option in the New Game menu to start that episode over, which will use the latest versions.
Major Feature: Directional Driving toggle

We’ve added new toggles in both Keyboard & Mouse and Gamepad menus for controlling your driving style. By default, on Keyboard & Mouse, it is enabled, and on Gamepad it is disabled. When disabled, your vehicle’s turning is always controlled by your left/right movement inputs rather than being controlled by your camera.
Note that this option does not affect vehicles with treads - those always use “tank controls” (since they are literally a tank)!

Hello,
thank you all for playing the Kinetic Update Beta and thank you for all of the reports and feedback!
In this week we have been working through the first batch and can provide an hotfix for the most pressing issues.
We appreciate all of the support during this Public Beta!
Developer Note on Crossovers, Track Connections & Industries Floating:

Crossovers - We looked into this further and have watched some of your videos of the issues that gave us some insights to what is happening. Looking at the footage, we found that when building crossover, you need to make sure that all tracks reaching the crossover are properly linked to the crossover.
The new spline system expects all tracks to be linked together, if there are any gaps or unconnected pieces or overlaps it will treat is as end of track and derail.
We suggest that you inspect your crossovers and relay all tracks on each side of the crossovers, from our testing we were able to glide over them without issue.

Track Snapping - With the change to the underlying spline system the game now checks for curve sharpness when laying rails. Meaning if you are laying a rail that is considered too steep < 30 Degrees the game will not display the snap link for you to connect to existing track. Curves have to be at a minimum of 30 degrees in order for the snap links to show up.

Industries Floating - Due to a legacy system being removed many of you noticed that some industries have started floating above the ground, this is noticeable on the Coalmine and the Sawmill to name a couple. If you are experiencing this issue, you can remove the industries and replace this, this will allow them to sit properly on the ground, then future loads will be unaffected.
We have added an auto fireman feature; it will automatically take fuel from the tenders and put it into the fireboxes. This feature is available for all fuel settings, except for "Realistic" (WIP)

items.text: Update 1.012 is now out on Steam, keepers.
Among the various bug fixes, QoL features and performance improvements, we’d like to highlight just a few that we think are pretty big and cool!

Previously, the PR Machine was a chore, and once your PR campaign started, there was nothing you could do to the machine itself. In this update, we decided to change how you run these campaigns and provide you with more flexibility.
First and foremost, you can now fully automate the process! No more tedious back-and-forth runs to reload it with the required items.

Now, all you need to do is just load the machine with the Hypno-devices and Newspapers in any quantity and run the campaigns for as long as needed (provided you have enough items for this period!). The machine will automatically use these items from the queue.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46076082/373c2bcbc1780a7215b7a9499016ca4b5c0eba79.gif"]

Also, you can now improve your PR Machine on any given day using just the Graveyard quality points. This is another reason for you to look after your graveyard – you are the Keeper and not just a propagandist after all!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46076082/7516b731109e5fa4c50b4b83cff9285283a8fa3e.gif"]
To balance it all out, you still need to load the items on the exact day. We just couldn’t simplify it THAT much, sorry.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46076082/d40554a6f7165d6d2e040c7ad12f615e6a4750ad.png"]

notes.title: More options to rest and pass time

items.text: In addition to sleep, you can now also sit on the bench by the campfire next to the Keeper’s house to restore energy and skip time. Cozy, innit?
Bear in mind that this does not save your progress or remove insanity and the ‘Lack of Sleep’ debuff. Once your energy is fully restored, you can keep sitting for as long as you like.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46076082/472ee0dc938d6814901dd3de17f991804fcc6c5e.gif"]

To make your life a little bit easier, and save you a few runs around the world, the Map now provides you with a lot more useful information at hand. For example, you can see how many bodies are stored in your morgue, the amount of current and max available zombies, or available order numbers.

releases.displayName: The Dawn’s Children are ready to fight! New features of the November update

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/e68f9abd26ca80a18503bad19b62c3a8523f7067.png"]

Hello, survivors! In this entry, we continue to tell you about the new parts created by the Dawn’s Children. This time, we’ll take a look at the legendary plasma cutter and the epic hover/wheel. Let’s dive in!

We remind you that all the new features described in the “Developer blog” are not final and may be changed before they are introduced into the game or may not make it into the game at all. This also applies to all visual materials.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/ae881ddb4b73a54e206c5764296670cfc3611b05.jpg"]
“Orthogon” is short for orthogonal, by the way. If you know, you know. The name is a perfect fit for a weapon that can rotate 90°.

“Orthogon” is a legendary successor to the “Blockchain”. As its predecessor, it also has a wide beam of heated plasma that can hit enemies immediately after a short charge. But the new cutter also has three new features: it can heat up parts, increase its own damage upon a successful hit, and rotate its barrel 90°! After the rotation, the beam it fires becomes vertical.

The weapon has two firing modes, horizontal and vertical. You need to rapidly press the fire button twice to switch between the modes by rotating the barrel 90°. With each subsequent switch, the barrel will continue to rotate in a circle with each turn being 90°. The weapon deals energy damage, but each hit also heats up enemy parts.

“Orthogon’s” unique feature is its charge accumulation. With every hit on an enemy, the cutter accumulates charge, and when fully charged, turning the barrel provides three amplified shots. These shots have increased damage, width, and heating. The amplified shots also accumulate charge, but for the other firing mode. Therefore, every hit contributes to the next turning, and the cycle repeats.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/8d0772c0c3091bf8f15e04f837bcd98404791ed2.jpg"]

The new movement part is reminiscent of Phaethon’s chariot. It won’t get you close to the sun but can still lift you up above the Wasteland. It also is visually similar to the wheels of a car from a famous film about time travel.
The movement part has two modes: a wheel and a hover. It starts out as a wheel, which can rotate and fly like a hover upon activation.

The “Phaethon’s” unique feature is related to its wheel mode. In this mode, the maximum speed limit is removed, and at the same time, hover power is boosted by a certain percentage. For every few meters traveled on the ground, the length of this boost increases by a certain amount of time, up to several times the initial duration.

releases.displayName: Dev Blog | Visional Wheel S5 "Dissonant Resonance" Foresight

items.text: Dear Metas,

Deep in the Nova, a colossal face gazes down upon the land. An unfamiliar frequency pierces through the ruins, weaving joy, enrage, sorrow, and fear into a single score—not a blessing for this world, but the final movement of destruction that the new Great One, "The Echo," seeks to perform.

The Visional Wheel spins once more. This time, the clue to confronting the Vision lies hidden within scattered Notes. Defeat the Deviants modified by the power of notes, rearrange and purify the broken Score, and turn the enemy's power into your own melody. As the Gulped in the sky casts its gaze, brave Metas will respond to this "performance" from the unknown in their own way.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/12/798ba4a810be46398256ac2bd891e2d8.png&code=YjRzVmgzdEtfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMg==" style="max-width:100%;"]
Opening Time
Opens after the November 18, 2026 （PT ）version update

Manibus (excluding Novice Scenario), Evolution's Call, Prismverse's Clash, The Way of Winter, Endless Dream, Deviation: Survive, Capture, Preserve, and Isles of Abyss. Metas can switch to the "Vision" world via the Worldstone to experience it.

Where The Echo's "Gospel" spreads, the will of fallen beings clings desperately to this land, transforming into a colossal calamity that yearns to speak—the Dissonant Husk. This Gulped suspended in the sky is composed of structures resembling copper pipes, its human-like yet inhuman face sending chills down the spine. Its massive form looms over the earth like a false god, and occasionally it notices the ant-like Metas below. Who says a "god" can't be amused by ants?

When Metas enter the Fundamental Tone Range and activate the Echo Bell, the Dissonant Husk reveals four faces across different regions—Delight, Wrath, Lament, and Terror—gazing upon every Meta who dares to intrude beneath an alien sky.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/10/874c66d4584349728de6613fdd1d3885.gif&code=U2tENHZwaTlfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]

"The Echo" was originally an ancient relic slumbering in the ruins. After the Nova Vision descended, the surface was vaporized and Stardust poured underground; the relic awakened within the Stardust, merging with collapsed pipes and ancient instruments to become what it is now. No one can establish contact with it—all researchers who entered the region have gone missing. It merely emits a low, repeating hum, as if performing an unfinished overture.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/13/6fffc37367f3457287500f7f4c377f08.png&code=OGtaanNNeW1fMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]

notes.title: Game Mode 1 - Resonant Movements: Use the reticle to pick up Notes and let the melody fall into place line by line

items.text: Ever since Stardust poured into the Pioneer's acoustic ruins, the awakened "Echo" has loathed the clamor of the world. With storming sounds, it tears through space-time, condensing Phase Anchor Fundamental Tone Ranges, and drives the Dissonant Army—infused with dissonant notes—through the passages into Nalcott, spreading its "gospel" everywhere in an attempt to drag all beings into a hall of extreme emotion and destruction.
1. Ring the Echo Bell to begin your Movement

During the Vision, four types of Resonant Movements game mode regions will appear across Nalcott: Movement of Delight, Movement of Wrath, Movement of Lament, and Movement of Terror. Each movement region differs in difficulty and rules.
After entering the region, interact with the \[Echo Bell] to start the Movement challenge. At this point, Metas will also receive a Score awaiting tuning.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/12/b056e855aa0c48c39cbce20ac9b4fa71.gif&code=WlJNRnc4ZHdfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]
2. Defeat the Dissonant Army and Tune the Score

Defeat Dissonant Army enemies carrying notes, and the corresponding notes will appear in the scene. Metas must refer to the prompts on the current score and fire at the required notes to fill them in sequence.

Notes will remain in the scene for a period of time and will give a prompt when they are about to disappear. When different notes appear simultaneously, accurately identifying and selecting them is just as important as killing speed.

Each Meta obtains their own notes and progresses their own score independently—they won't lose their chance to obtain notes because another Meta shot them. Everyone can clear enemies together, then each complete their own melody.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/13/9ee29a3ed9d14432a533df0e0df74e0f.png&code=azlueGJYVURfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]
3. Protect your Score Progress and complete the final signature
Each time you complete a line of the score, you'll receive the corresponding Phase Rewards. As the blanks are gradually filled in, the originally dissonant movement will become whole once again.

As the battle reaches its final stage, the Dissonant Emissary carrying the Movement Signature will become an opponent you must face. That is the key to completing the entire movement, and also an extension of The Echo's will within the soundscape.

After achieving victory on the battlefield and completing your personal score, Metas will receive a Legendary Movement. Use it to listen to the full piece and claim rewards; if your personal score is not yet complete when you achieve battlefield victory, you will receive an Incomplete Movement and claim a smaller corresponding reward.

notes.title: Game Mode 2 - The Echo War: Face The Echo in Nova

items.text: [img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/13/f0beaa13d9a54b6cbd270f7bece560d8.png&code=UjlmQ2ppSnpfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]
Fifteen minutes after the Vision begins, The Echo will descend directly upon Nalcott in avatar form. Metas can enter The Echo War through The Echo's portal shown on the map.

The Echo War supports up to 4 players in a team and takes the form of a separate Dungeon. Metas, please make full preparations before entering. The Echo War also has two difficulty levels: Basic and Hard. Please choose the difficulty that suits you.

The Echo has multiple attack forms, such as sound wave attacks, summoning minions, wide-area impacts, and more. Metas must watch for battlefield cues, use the interactions in the arena to counter threats, and seize the moments when The Echo reveals its weakspots to focus fire. Promptly handling interference and responding to mechanics, then unleashing firepower during key windows, is a crucial part of this confrontation.
1. Dissonant Dust

Dissonant Dust is the crystallized form of The Echo's dissonant movement fragments, retaining lingering traces of bygone noise. This item can be used to open the Resonance Box, and can also be exchanged for certain items in the Visional Redemption Shop.

Metas can obtain Dissonant Dust through Vision-related game modes such as Resonant Movements and The Echo War, as well as the Visional Wheel event. This item has a weekly acquisition cap; once the cap is reached, the acquisition rate will decrease.
2. Resonance Box

The Resonance Box is a sonic crystallization left in the world by The Echo. It comes in three rarities: Epic, Legendary, and Mythic. The higher the rarity, the more precious the rewards. Opening a Resonance Box guarantees Divine Rhythm, though the exact amount varies. There is also a chance to obtain rare rewards such as precious Mods and high-level Deviations.
Metas can also consume varying amounts of Dissonant Dust to perform different tiers of Resonance. Among them, \[Deep Resonance] has a chance to grant double rewards!
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/13/8c138cda801f4776810047e77ac540af.png&code=UmxQVllwWVlfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]
3. Divine Rhythm

Divine Rhythm is an exclusive item obtained when opening Resonance Boxes. After collecting Divine Rhythm, you can visit Event - Visional Redemption - Redeem Shop to redeem precious rewards such as Lightforge Ingots, selected Shop Fashion/Furniture/Weapon Skins, Shiny Mods, top-tier Deviations, and more.
4. Special Adjustments to This Season's Visional Shop
To meet Metas' redemption needs, this season's Visional Redemption Shop will add limited redemption opportunities for select past Visional Mod Crates.
New Combat Deviation: Silent Statue O-079

Deviation O-079 is a grayish-white stone humanoid statue, approximately 1.7 meters tall and weighing about 480 kg. The entire statue is covered in fine radial patterns that begin at O-079-A and spread along both arms across the whole body. Material analysis identifies it as ordinary granite, but all sampling attempts have ended in failure: drill bits shatter approximately 2 mm into the surface, with the fracture surfaces alternately showing traces of high-temperature melting and rapid freezing. The face is a blank, uncarved surface.

A spherical silence zone with a radius of approximately 15 meters surrounds O-079. Sound waves cannot propagate within this zone, and those who enter immediately notice that "the world has been muted". However, personnel inside the silence zone can still converse normally—post-incident interviews indicate that what they heard was not each other's voices. The vast majority of those affected describe the experience as "a choir without lyrics" and unanimously agree that its source is "in the sky".

O-079's primary Deviation trait is its periodic spreading fluctuation. From time to time, O-079-A emits a ring of visible ripples outward (hereinafter referred to as O-079-B). Wherever the ripples pass, all things briefly experience a violent Wrath of Nature—be it scorching heat, extreme cold, or crawling lightning. These three calamities cycle endlessly, with their order and intervals entirely unpredictable. Living targets touched by O-079-B are often left covered in wounds, yet those who have long accompanied it remain unharmed, as if the ripples recognize them.

Note that O-079 continuously spreads its "gospel" indiscriminately. Personnel who remain within its area of influence for extended periods will hear the lyrics of a choir in their dreams and report thoughts such as "Mother is watching us from the sky" along with an impulse to reach toward the sky. This mental influence subsides within approximately 3 weeks after breaking contact, with no permanent cases recorded.
Battle Skill "Elemental Shift"

Automatically cycles among three Keyword Effects: Burn, Power Surge, and Frost Vortex. When the battle skill is cast, a spreading wave is emitted centered on the target, dealing corresponding Status DMG and applying the Keyword Effect;
Ultimate "Elemental Resonance"

Summons a Silent Statue to bestow blessings upon the Metas. Each time an enemy receives an Elemental Keyword Effect, the Statue gains the corresponding Elemental Resonance, increasing Status DMG for the summoner and their teammates within range. Collecting all three Resonances greatly increases the Keyword DMG Rate.
How to Obtain
The Silent Statue can mainly be obtained by participating in The Echo War, and can also be obtained through the Visional Shop (current season) and by opening the Resonance Box.
After the current Vision season ends, this Deviation will be added to the standard Game Mode drop pool. Please refer to future announcements for details.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/10/7f78c565b388468a9b60978154785b2a.gif&code=NVJrOU9IOExfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]
Morphed Deviation
This update adds three new Morphed Deviations: Artisan's Touch - Dissonant Resonance, Wish Box - Dissonant Resonance, and Gazocchio - Dissonant Resonance.
How to Obtain

Morphed Deviations can mainly be obtained by participating in Resonant Movements, The Echo War, and Vision events. They can also be obtained through the Visional Shop (current season) and by opening the Resonance Box.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/13/b75c64dbdb494fe795aa7f4187c47af5.png&code=SHI4MG9JWUdfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]
Suffix
Increases Weapon DMG. Increases further when HP is high.
Increases Crit DMG. Increases further when HP is high.

Increases damage dealt to all enemies.

[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/13/d3aeea76b62f4a7cb5d40b6b0bfe0098.png&code=aXB4WE1KRWVfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxMw==" style="max-width:100%;"]

Previously, the Bastille Set had harsh trigger and maintenance conditions, making it difficult to perform reliably in common combat. This adjustment relaxes the trigger and maintenance conditions for the Bastille state and adds a continuous recovery effect during combat, alleviating the HP cap suppression caused by low sanity and allowing Metas to handle certain combat environments with greater ease.
[table equalcells="1" colwidth=","]
Set Pieces
Effect
1 Piece
When HP is high, Weapon DMG and Status DMG are increased.
2 Pieces
Reload Efficiency is increased.

After completing a reload or using a healing syringe, enter the Bastille state for a duration. During Bastille, Weapon DMG and Status DMG are increased, with an additional boost when HP is high. Hitting an enemy refreshes the duration of the Bastille state.

During Bastille, the Max HP reduction from low sanity is alleviated, and you continuously gain armor. When armor is at max stacks, consume all armor to restore a portion of HP and gain an equal amount of shield.

We have observed that the synergy between Tactical Combat Boots and the SN700 - Finale allows Finale to continuously fire multiple enhanced tail bullets, which somewhat exceeded our expectations for Finale's power ceiling. Additionally, considering server performance and the multiplayer alpha battle experience in the wilderness, this update adjusts the auto-loading mechanism of Tactical Combat Boots.
[table equalcells="1" colwidth=","]

While in Fortress Warfare, consume Bullet Stock every 2.5 seconds to randomly refill 1–10 bullets. Fire Rate boosts by 15%.

Events accompanying the Vision will also revolve around gameplay experience and phase objectives, allowing everyone to accumulate rewards as they gradually become familiar with the Movements. Metas can challenge different emotional Echoes in the Tone Range combat, complete the hero's challenge, or collect various Echo Scores to complete the scattered Scores of "The Echo".
Click "Event Interface - Visional Wheel" to participate in the current Vision-related events. The following content will be available this season:
Dissonant Resonance: Metas can learn about the basic rules for this Vision and claim rewards on this page.

Movement Rotation: A weekly event. Challenge each region of the main game mode of this Vision, "Resonant Movements," to accumulate Active Progress and earn rewards such as Weapon Skins and Lightforge Ingots.
Movement Collection: Collect and listen to various scores from different emotional Movements through the Resonant Movements Game Mode. Earn rare rewards based on Collection Progress.
Echoes into Verses: Accumulate Progress by collecting Dissonant Dust to obtain precious rewards such as rare Territory Collectibles and Character Namecard Themes.
Tuning Journey: Complete the Vision's achievement challenges to earn rare rewards such as Mod Crates and Deviations.
Specific event rules, reward content, and claim conditions will be explained in subsequent announcements and on the in-game event page.
[img src="https://office.netease.com/api/pub/file/download?path=popo/2026/11/13/aab1f6f383544c1db1c69e736e63f0f5.png&code=WUFGT28wbDhfMTc5NDU2MzY2MzUxNA==" style="max-width:100%;"]

As the S5 Visional Wheel opens, the S4 Vision \[Gravity Abyss] will also come to an end. The S4 Visional Redemption Shop will close on December 2 PT. Metas, please make sure to open your corresponding \[Abyssal Cores] in time and redeem your remaining \[Gravity Crystals] and \[Abyssal Essence].
After the Shop closes, unredeemed \[Abyssal Essence] and \[Gravity Crystals] can no longer be used. Please keep track of the time to avoid any losses.
On November 18（ PT）, Visional Wheel S5 \[Dissonant Resonance] opens. Let us rescore the lost movement in the frequency of The Echo.

That's all for this Dev Blog. Metas, you are welcome to share your experiences and thoughts with us through the Feedback Platform (Once Human Feedback Platform). Thank you all for your continued support, and we look forward to meeting you again in \[Dissonant Resonance].
Once Human Development Team

items.text: Hey everybody,
We’ve seen that you have been asking about what to expect from A Little to the Left this Summer, and we’re pleased to finally tell you about the free Packed Update, coming June 26th!

We’re introducing new levels, modes and improvements, all neatly packaged into our final major update. It launches later this week on PC, Mac, Switch, Xbox and PlayStation, and mobile versions will also receive the free update very soon.

releases.displayName: Dev Diary #29: FREE Wolf Update Patch Notes

items.text: Hello everyone! This is a joint Dev Diary by Jordi, QA Specialist and Tom, Lead Designer. Today we’re going to be talking about the Wolf Update which is coming out on February 27th with the Primal Fury content pack. Everything in this update is free, you just need the base game to get it!
In the golem update we added the War Coordination system for vassal cities. In this update we’ve brought similar functionality for coordinating attacks with other rulers in the form of Bounties!

Bounties are Ruler created quests that can be offered in exchange for a reward. Any non-hostile Rulers may choose to accept your Bounty. The Ruler that completes the objective within the given timeframe will receive the reward and complete the Bounty.
Bounties can be made and managed in the Quest Overview.
Bounties can target Cities and Victory structures that are viable for other Rulers and offer a reward for achieving the bounty
Multiple rulers may accept the bounty, but only the Ruler that completes it will receive the reward.
AI Rulers can post Bounties for completion. Accepting these will add them to your Quest Tracker and completing them will see you earn the Reward.
AI Rulers that accept bounties will send messages giving updates on how their attacks are going.

As well as adding new content to the Pantheon system, we’ve done a big pass on the tech, flow and gameplay aspects. The main goal for this update is to make Ascended Rulers feel more special, by granting them a special trait when they complete a realm, and allowing them to keep their racial transformations. We’ve also added logic for an ascended ruler to remember the tomes they collected during the game, so that the AI can pick the same tomes again if it takes control of them!
Ruler Management
Once a custom ruler ascends, they will now be moved into the pantheon and out of the custom rulers list.
A new tab featuring all the pantheon rulers is now visible in faction creation and selection.
Pantheon rulers can now be edited and campaign rulers (when not edited manually) will automatically update to the latest settings.
Removing a pantheon ruler will place it back in the custom rulers list (if it was a custom ruler).
Already ascended rulers can ascend again to update their recorded information and race transformations.

Pantheon Rulers gained from Story Realms now default to act as Rulers and not as recruitable heroes. Only applies to newly ascended campaign rulers, you can always change this setting in the pantheon screen.
A warning has been added when a ruler is worthy to ascend but the maximum rulers in the pantheon has already been reached on finishing a session (already ascended rulers may ascend again however).
Ascension
Added 26 Ascension Traits. One trait can be chosen at the end of a game upon ascensions of a Ruler.
The Traits one can choose from are based on your Affinity and the Tomes chosen during the game.
If you ascend again, you can choose a new trait to replace the original one.
When conquering a Realm your applied Transformations are maintained. Your Ruler will be under the effects of these Transformations when next played by you or an AI.
Ascended Champions gain the choice to not partake in new Transformations cast during a Game.
Dragon Lords will benefit from their Aspect skill, their Transformation remains dormant until the appropriate level has been reached.
When conquering a Realm your researched Tomes will be remembered and when this ruler is next played by an AI that AI Ruler will attempt to research the same Tomes as you originally did.
A new option has been added to Advanced Setup to disable the Ascension mechanics and bonuses during a session.
Prevents rulers from starting with ascension traits, transformations and skills.
Pantheon rulers will not show up as heroes during a session.
On winning the session, your ruler will not ascend.
New Pantheon Content
Added New Pantheon Rewards
Crow Master’s Bow Hero Origin
Druidic Terraformers
Primal Good Banner Icon
Primal Evil Banner Icon
Keeper’s Helmet
Marauder Helmet
6 Mount Visualisations
Lion
Panther
Tiger
Stag
Zebra
Warhound
Added 8 new events for Pantheon Godir that can join the player as heroes.
2 alignment based events
6 affinity based events.
Increased the rarity of Pantheon Hero events, which should increase the chance of a pantheon hero event showing.

When looking at how the hero cap worked, we became unhappy with how it interacted with acquiring new cities. Since getting more cities and getting more heroes were both very strong strategic approaches, having them intrinsically linked by saying that each city grants an extra hero was making the game’s meta very narrow, since simply grabbing as many cities as possible was the only viable approach.

The new system disconnects heroes from cities, allowing you to spend imperium to speed up acquiring more. This means players must choose between using imperium to have lots of cities OR lots of heroes, rather than always getting both.

Alongside these changes comes a new interaction between Heroes that are part of the same Stack. We felt that multi-hero stack armies were undermining the core idea of the game, by reducing the importance of normal units in armies. To try and counter this we’ve added a penalty that stacks the more heroes are within a single army.
The hero cap now increases over time instead of being linked to the number of cities. The first hero cap increase happens in 10 turns, subsequent increases each take 5 turns longer.
The hero cap can be instantly increased in the hero overview screen by spending imperium.
You can no longer recruit heroes beyond the hero cap.
When integrating a free city, their ruler will no longer be given directly, instead their ruler will become recruitable (for free) in the recruitment screen.
Existing save games will automatically upgrade to the new system and set the current cap to either be based on the current turn number or the number of cities the player has (whichever is higher).
Added “Leadership Clash” to all Heroes and Rulers. This will reduce the Morale and XP gain for heroes, if more than one hero is in an army

The base game’s version of Necromancy wasn’t quite where we wanted it to be in terms of player experience. In too many respects it felt like all the other styles of magic, and wasn’t really hitting the goal of making you feel like the master of an ever growing army of the dead.

To address this we’ve been doing some major reworking of the necromancy tomes, giving them a focus of spending souls to directly reanimate the enemies you slay as skeletons under your command. Using an early game piece of research you can start bringing back normal racial units as skeletons, with the type of skeleton you raise based on the unit that you slayed. So instead of just having a bunch of skeletons with pikes, you can now have skeletons with swords and shields, bows and even skeletal mages. Later on you can start raising more powerful creatures as Bone Horrors and Bone Dragons too!
We’ve made a raft of other changes as well to smooth out the experience, and boost the power level of the tomes which many felt were lacking when compared to other tome lines.
General
Lowered soul gain per kill from 2/3/4/5/6 to 1/2/3/4/5.
Soul rewards on kill are now granted during combat, allowing you to spend Souls on spells immediately.
Soulbound now also causes a unit to have a 30% chance to transform into a Decaying Zombie under your control until the end of combat when it dies.
Constructing Skeletons no longer comes with any Necromancy Tome. Instead you can now use the three new Reanimation Skills to raise undead units after combat.
Post Combat Raising

Researching the appropriate Reanimation Skill, allows you to raise fallen units as Undead. After combat you're presented with a list of Units that can be raised, any amount of them can be selected provided you have the Souls. The system uses all units that entered the battle on the Enemy side and have died to determine which units are able to be raised as undead.
This means it does not interfere with the capture or mind control conditions since those units need to stay alive.
This means that units that have been summoned or have routed are not valid.
You buy these units using Souls.
When killing Racial Units of any tier (15 Souls - requires Skeleton Reanimation)
You will always get a Tier 1 skeleton that costs 15 Souls. But depending on what the role was of the unit that is killed, you can raise one of 4 different types of skeletons as follows:
Shield (Shield, Fighter, Hero)
Polearm (Polearm, Shock)
Archer (Ranged, Skirmisher)
Battle Mage (Battle Mage, Support)
When killing non-racial units
Tier 3-4: Tier 3 Bone Horror (50 Souls - requires Bone Horror Reanimation)
Tier 5: Tier 4 Bone Dragon (100 Souls - requires Bone Dragon Reanimation)
Tome Updates
Tome of Necromancy
Now a Tier I Tome
New Skill “Skeleton Reanimation” - Empire Bonus that allows you to raise Tier 1 skeleton units from slain racial units after combat. The unit that you can raise depends on the role it had:
Shield Skeleton (Shield, Fighter, Hero)
Polearm Skeleton (Polearm, Shock)
Archer Skeleton (Ranged, Skirmisher)
Battle Mage Skeleton (Battle Mage, Support)
New Combat Spell “Necrotize”
Target Unit sustains 10 Frost/10 Blight Damage
Target Unit becomes Decaying
Summons a Decaying Zombie under your Control on Unit Death
Necromancer - Now a Tier 2 Support unit instead of T3.
Combat Spell “Rotting Explosion” - Can now also target skeleton units
Unit Enchantment “Necrotic Magic” - Increased upkeep from 2 to 3 Mana
Hero Skill “Unholy Leader” - Now also increases the resistance of Undead units in the army by 1.
The following skills were moved to the Tier II Tome.
Special Province Improvement “Soulwell” - Increased Soulwell Income from 3 to 5
World Map Spell “Soul Collection” - Increased income from 6 to 10
The following skills were moved to the Tome of Souls
World Map Spell “Restore Undead”
World Map Spell “Summon Corrupt Soul”
The following skills were removed
Combat Spell “Raise Zombies”
Tome of Souls
Now a Tier II Tome
New Skill “Bone Horror Reanimation” - Empire Bonus that allows you to raise non-racial T3-4 units as Bone Horrors after combat.
The Bone Horror is now a Tier 3 unit instead of a T2.
The Bone Horror unit no longer transforms into Skeletons on death.
The Bone Horror unit now spawns a Zombie unit when its HP drops under 50%.
Unit Enchantment “Soulbinders” - Increased additional damage against Soulbound units from 10% to 20%.
Hero Skill “Soul Collector” - Increased additional damage against Soulbound units from 10% to 20%.
The following skills were moved from the Tome of Necromancy
World Map Spell “Restore Undead” - Renamed to Restore Undead Army.
World Map Spell “Summon Corrupt Soul”
The following skills were moved to the Tome of Necromancy
Combat Spell “Soul Overflow”
World Map Spell “Soul Collection”
The following skills were removed
Combat Spell “Soul Fire”
Tome of the Great Transformation
New Skill: Bone Dragon Reanimation - Empire Bonus that allows you to raise Bone Dragons from T5 units after combat.
Tome of the Reaper
Unit “Reaper”:
Added the Ethereal Unit Type
Melee Strike
Changed from 20 Physical damage to 10 Physical and 10 Frost damage
Added Piercing - Ignores 50% of the target's Defense
Added Breaching - Ignores 50% of the target’s Resistance
Finger of Death
Changed from a Full action to a Single Action ability
Reduced Range from 4 to 3
The 45 Frost damage from failing to kill now ignores all resistance the target has.
Dark Rites - Now grants the Reaper 1 Strengthened and 10 Hp for each enemy that dies in battle. Doesn’t count Summons, Siegecraft and Towers.
Now displays a property that tells that it has a 5 Soul Upkeep but a -50% Mana and Gold upkeep
Siege Project “Construct Soul Siphons” - Now applies Soulbound to all enemies and deals 3 fortification damage
World Map Spell “Harvest Population” - Increased Soul Income from +10 to +30.
Combat Spell “Mark for Death”
Renamed to “Marked for Death”
Target unit:
Sustains 15 unblocked Physical Damage
Loses 10 Morale
Has a decaying zombie appear adjacent to them
Gains a Debuff called Visions of Death that triggers the above 3 effects at the end of each turn.
Combat Spell “Greater Reanimation”
Reduced the Soul Cost of this spell from 35 Souls to 20.
Revives Undead units with 100% of their Hit Points
Revives non-undead units as Corrupt Souls.
Enemy Undead units and Corrupt Souls gained in combat with this spell can be purchased for Souls at the end of combat if they survive.
Tome of the Eternal Lord:
Unit Enchantment “True Death Magic”
No longer applies Marked for Death
Now grants an ability called ‘Curse of the Reaper’, a Full Action ability which cares about engagement in close combat version of the Finger of Death ability from the Reaper unit.
As well as the above balance changes, we’ve been working hard to bring you a whole host of quality of life changes!
Added Random Realm/Realm Trait Randomization
You can now get the system to generate a randomized realm for you, if you don’t feel like picking out a realm’s traits for yourself.
Added new Free City Upgrades
Free cities will now start making use of tome units in the late game, instead of only culture units. These tome units will also be available to the city’s masters via the rally of lieges!
Added Dismantle Province Operation
It’s now possible to dismantle a city’s provinces, if you want to switch their territory to cover a different area. Only provinces on the edge of a City are eligible for dismantling.
Added Enchantment & Transformation Visual Toggle

We’ve added functionality to the spell book that lets you hide the visual effects of unit enchantments and transformations. This means you can have better control of what your race looks like when you take multiple, overlapping transformations or enchantments. It also means you can take a transformation for its mechanical effect, without needing to have it visually update your forces.
For technical reasons, transformations that give you wings (Angelize and Demonkin) or replace your legs (Naga Transformation) cannot be disabled.
Faction Creation Improvements
We’ve added the option to explicitly specify a name for the faction’s starting city, as well as rewrite the faction’s biography, so you can make a faction more your own.
Also, to reduce some confusion, it is now possible to overwrite an existing faction when you edit it (previously you only had the option to save your edited faction as a new one)
UI Updates

Added brand new Parchment Images, just because they look cool!
And that’s about it for big new things! Obviously we’ve also made a huge assortment of balance changes, bug fixes and general improvements, all of which you can read about in detail:
The Wolf Update will roll out across all platforms on February 27th, along with the brand new Primal Fury content pack!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/e04b1812e019f05cc994f8e4c4eb7f5686b46323.png"]
Hello everyone!
Rise from Ruin and the accompanying Scorpion update are coming in less than a week - next Monday, 9th of March! Read the patch notes to find out what is to come:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/50e2d70ddb5c0f66d97ba5a2b95b9942581aae67.gif"]
Move Speed Normalization

All regular units now share the same number of Move Points on the World Map. This ensures that mixing slower and faster units in a single army no longer reduces the overall travel speed, allowing for higher army diversity and strategy.
All units now have 40 Move Points on the World Map
All Scout Units now have 48 Move Points on the World Map
Added Combat Speed, a new stat that indicates how many hexes per turn a unit can move in Combat.
Changed the rounding on the Combat Speed to Action Point Calculation. In most cases you will now have more action points when moving the same distance in pre-Scorpion.
Associated Updates
Form “Feline” - Now also has Elusive
Form “Lupine” - Now also has Ferocious
Form Trait “Athletics”
Now only increased Combat Speed
Reduced Cost from 2 Points to 1 Point
Form Trait “Mount Masters” - Additional Effect: +5 HP to Mounted units.
Form Trait “Hardy” - Increased HP from +8 to +10
All Non-Flying Exotic Mount Traits - Reduced Cost from 3 to 2
Beast Wrangler Ogre contracts for Land Mounts - Reduced Cost from 1000 Gold and 200 Imperium to 700 Gold and 140 Imperium
Floating and Flying units now spend 6 points per hex traveled instead of 5
Passive Infusion “Fast Movement” - Reduced Infusion Cost from 2 to 1
Passive Infusion “Very Fast Movement” - Reduced Infusion Cost from 3 to 2
Defense/Resistance Update

We’re updating how Defense and Resistance work across all units to bring them back in line with their original design intent. The new system changes how damage reduction is applied, focusing on the source of damage rather than the type of damage dealt. We’re also adding a new Unit Role that deals Magic Damage at Melee range, the Magic Fighter.
The Defense stat now reduces all Damage (including Magic Damage) from Abilities that have Melee or Physical Ranged tags
The Resistance stat now reduces all Damage (including Physical Damage) from Abilities that have the Magic tag and Spells
In the case that an attack would be blocked by both Defense and Resistance, the higher value is chosen.
Renamed Damage Channel Resistance to Damage Channel Protection
Damage Channel Protection is added to Defense or Resistance to determine final Damage Reduction
Added Damage Channel Protection: Physical
Rebalanced the stats of the core unit types - Most units have less resistance than defense, with exceptions for battle mages, support units and ranged units which have more resistance than defense.
Ability descriptors like Magic and Base now have tooltips that explain what they mean
New Unit Role: Magic Fighter
Uses Melee Range attacks that count as Magical called Magic Strike.
Have the Passive “Melee Mage” allowing for Ranged Magic Attacks to be used when engaged
Uses most Battle Mage Unit Enchantments and the defensive or generic Fighter Unit Enchantments.

Experience Update

All units now gain XP automatically each turn, even when not fighting. This means your armies will continue to improve simply by existing and participating in your empire. XP gained from battles has been halved which means Units still get rewarded for combat, but fighting is no longer the only reliable way to level up. With this we’re also bringing back Exalted Ranks. Once a unit reaches its final rank, it can continue leveling up indefinitely.

All Units now have a passive Experience gain of 10 XP per Turn

Certain Hand-crafted regions with specific themes, such as the Sunless and Blessed regions, now only show up in specific Realm Traits, such as Sunless Highlands and Blessed Fields. The only hand-crafted regions that can always show up in a realm are the ones from Giant Kings and the Desert hand-crafted regions from Rise from Ruin.

Added new Misc Trait "Sunless Regions” - Adds several Sunless Regions, the Thorn Heart Landmark and Blood Glass Material to your Realm

The Beginner Realm no longer spawns Umbral infestations to make it easier for the player, as both introduce a level of complexity with the fact that they spread a negative terrain with their infestation domain.

Changed the rebuilding of the borders to only trigger on excavating sectors since this is the only terraforming effect that really changes the height of the map. Optimizing all other instances of terraforming.
Improved the generation of the Umbral Abyss when playing without the underground enabled.
The “Capture and Release Ancient Wonder” action no longer removes a unit’s move points. The units are free to move on while the action is running.
It is now possible to use Force March on individual units of a stack

This is done by first selecting the units of the stack by clicking their portraits and then giving a move order by right clicking the map as usual. After confirming the Force March popup only the selected units will receive the effects.

Water Improvements
Water has long been the least rewarding part of the map: costly to enter, limiting in combat, and visually flat. This update takes on all three, on the world map, in battle and on screen.
World Map Gameplay
Embarking now has a flat cost, Outposts can be founded on water provinces, and the Random Map Generator has been retuned so oceans shape the layout of a realm.
Movement & Settlement
Renamed terrain types: Ocean is now Deep Ocean, Coastal is now Ocean and Water is now Underground Water.
Changed the cost of embarking a unit from all of its Movement Points (minimum 12) to a flat 20 Movement Points.
Added the same +2 Vision granted to Embarked Units to Aquatic Units.
Added founding Outposts on habitable provinces with water in the center. These Outposts cannot be converted into Cities, except by the Mercantile Culture.
Added building the Spelljammer, Beacon of Unity and Teleporter Special Province Improvements on water provinces.
Random Map Generator
Continents
Increased ocean size and made continents more consistent in size, so the sea plays a bigger role in how a realm is laid out.
Changed continents belonging to AI players so they can connect to each other by land, instead of always being separated by water.
Changed AI players to no longer be placed on a shared continent with another player by default. Human players still start on a shared continent so they can reach each other early.
Coastal: Changed the ocean to sit in one corner of the map instead of being spread around the edges, with fewer and smaller islands.
Divide: Removed the islands along the ocean that splits the two continents, and increased the width of that ocean considerably, so it reads as a proper ocean rather than a wide river.
Islands
Removed the Lava terrain overlay, removing unsightly lava/ocean borders.
Changed resource values: lower on land, higher on the ocean.
Combat Gameplay
Embarked units follow their own rules for turning and positioning, with stats adjusted to match, and summons, resurrections, transformations and teleports now work at sea.
Embarked
Added Large Target and Reinforced.
Added -2 Fire Protection.
Removed -2 Defense and -2 Resistance.
Removed the damage reduction due to casualties.
Added Limited Maneuverability to embarked units, Ghost Ships and Ironclads:
Units spend Movement Points each time they turn while moving.
Using the Rotate Unit Ability spends all of the unit's remaining Movement Points.
Units cannot use Opportunity Attacks or Retaliations against hexes behind them.
Added Amphibious Movement to Ironclads.
Abilities & Spells on Water

Added the Water Walk passive, which is granted in combat to any unit that cannot cross the current map's terrain on its own (for example a land unit summoned on a water map), allowing it to use land movement on water hexes.
Changed abilities and spells that summon, resurrect or transform units to work on water maps (with a few rare exceptions, mostly involving plants).
Changed magical teleport abilities (e.g. Teleportation) to work on water.
Changed non-magical teleport abilities (e.g. Disengage Unit) to only be blocked while the unit is embarked.
Changed Amphibious units to become Wet while on water.
Visual Improvements

Water rendering has been reworked for readability, every aquatic battle map has been redressed with new props and sea life, and ships now carry the look of the culture that sails them, with new skins in Faction Creation.
Ship Customization
Added 3 unique Boat Skins to choose from during Faction Creation: Default, Graceful and Brutal.
Added a default ship style for each culture.
Changed Free Cities to use the ships of their associated faction, Dwellings to use their own boats where available, and other independents to use Marauder ships.

Trade Routes

Trade Routes are a new economic system that connects your Cities to Outposts, Free Cities, and the Cities of other Empires. Each Route is built and owned by a single City, which receives the Route's income; what you gain depends on what the Route connects to. Routes can be raided in open war, and a new line of City structures lets you specialize a City around its trade.
General
Trade Routes are created from the Trade Route panel and are built through the Unit Production Queue.
A Trade Route's Draft cost depends on its target and distance.
Trade Route production can be hurried.
Creating a Trade Route requires the target City to have been explored.

notes.title: Trade Route capacity is per City

items.text: 1 Route by default.
+1 per core Trade structure (Trade Post, Trade Quarters, Trade Bazaar).
+1 from the Caravaneer's Guild.
+3 in every City when the Megacities realm trait is active, or when your faction has the Chosen Destroyers Society Trait.
Trade Routes are guarded by Trader Escorts. Escort strength depends on the City's Trade structures:
Base: 2× Tier 1.
Trade Post: 3× Tier 1, 1× Tier 2.
Trade Quarters: 3× Tier 1, 3× Tier 2.
Trade Bazaar: 1× Tier 1, 3× Tier 2, 2× Tier 3.
Trade Routes are automatically regenerated or destroyed when territory along their path changes owner. The City's owner receives a notification explaining what happened.
Trade Routes also regenerate automatically when a province along their path is terraformed.
Trade Routes that pass through territory the owner no longer has access to are rerouted.
Nomad Cities: Trade Routes are restored for free when the settler unpacks.
Province Improvement “Teleporter”
Changed Upkeep from a local Outpost upkeep to a global empire upkeep of 10 Mana, so it no longer interacts with Trade Route income.
Economy
Culture Trait “Tyrannical Exploitation” (Dark)
Reduced Bonus from 20% to 2% per allegiance, to account for the much larger income now gained from Vassals.
Changed to only apply to Vassal tribute when an active Trade Route to that Vassal exists.
Description - Updated to state the 2% bonus instead of the previous 20%.
Culture Trait “Potential of Growth” (Mystic) - Removed its effect on Outposts.
Culture Trait “Potential of Control” (Mystic) - Removed its effect on Outposts.
Empire Skill 9B “Absolute Loyalty” (Order) - Reduced the Income bonus from Supreme Vassalage from +40% to +20%.
Society Trait “Chosen Uniters” - Reduced Income Bonus from +30% to +10%.
Interface
Added a Trade Routes overlay toggle to the overview map.
Trade Routes are otherwise only visible when a City is selected, an army is standing on a Route, or the Economic Overview is open.
Trade Route income is listed under its own “Trade Route” entry in the City income overview.
Added Trade Route information to the Outpost panel, including whether a Trade Route is connected and, if so, to which City.
Added a combat preview for battles involving Trade Routes.
Added tooltips for Trade Routes, including while they are still in the production queue.
Notifications
Added a notification when a Trade Route is completed.
Added separate notifications, each with its own message and event icon, for when one of your Trade Routes is raided, removed or rerouted.
Added a Trade Route Income concept, linked from the Trade Route tutorial and the Trade Route concept.
City Structures

Three core Trade structures, unlocked by City tier, grow with the City. Each also offers a choice between two mutually exclusive sub-structures, so a City can lean toward Outposts and Free Cities or toward trade with other Empires.
Trade Post (Tier 2)
Requires Town Hall II.
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Increases the strength of Trade Route Escorts.
Grants +5 Gold to this City's owner for each Trade Route owned by another City that connects to this City.

notes.title: Unlocks one of the following (mutually exclusive)

items.text: Outpost Supply Hub
Outposts connected to this City by Trade Route provide +50% income.
Diplomatic Embassy
Each Trade Route with another Empire's City grants this City +5 Imperium.
Trade Quarters (Tier 3)
Requires Trade Post.
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Increases the strength of Trade Route Escorts.
Grants +10 Gold to this City's owner for each Trade Route owned by another City that connects to this City.

notes.title: Unlocks one of the following (mutually exclusive)

items.text: Food Importers
Each Trade Route with an Outpost or Free City grants this City +20 Food and +10 Stability.
Wizard's Exchange
Each Trade Route with another Empire's City grants this City +10 Knowledge and +10 Mana.
Trade Bazaar (Tier 4)
Requires Trade Quarters.
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Increases the strength of Trade Route Escorts.
Grants +15 Gold to this City's owner for each Trade Route owned by another City that connects to this City.

notes.title: Unlocks one of the following (mutually exclusive)

items.text: Caravaneer's Guild
+1 Trade Route Capacity.
Trade Routes cost 20% less Draft in this City.
Counts as a Guild; a City may only have one Guild.
Taxation Offices
Each Trade Route grants this City +5 Gold and +5 Stability.
Targets
Outposts
Outposts no longer have an economy of their own: a Trade Route makes an Outpost an extension of the connected City, sending everything its Domain produces there.
Outposts no longer cost 10 Gold upkeep.
Outposts provide no income until connected by a Trade Route.
An Outpost connected by a Trade Route sends all Local and Global income from its Domain to the connected City.
Each Outpost can only be connected to one City.
Outposts no longer receive Resource Sharing. This closes an exploit where Corrupt Pact would also grant its Food bonus to Outposts connected by a Trade Route.
Free Cities
Free Cities normally pay Tribute in Gold and Mana only. A Trade Route opens up their full output, Local resources included, and lets you steer what they produce through Trade Focuses.
A Trade Route can be established with any Free City you have at least a Pact of Cooperation with.
Base Free City Tribute (without a Trade Route) is capped at 10% of its Gold and Mana income.
Trade Route income from a Free City is a percentage of its income, set by your diplomatic state with it:
War: 5%
Pact of Cooperation: 5%
Pact of Loyalty: 10%
Establishing a Trade Route to a Free City grants +100 Relation with it.

notes.title: Trade Focuses replace the old Free City trade options

items.text: Available with any Free City you have a Trade Route with.
Costs Imperium per turn (5 at base) and lasts until cancelled.
Increases the Free City's output of the chosen resource by 50%, raising the income supplied through the Route.
Only one Focus can be active per Free City; the available options depend on the resources it produces.
Trade Focus treaties can be cancelled from the Diplomacy Overview screen.
Magic Material trades remain available.
Foreign Cities
With a Free Trade Agreement in place, two Empires can build Routes into each other's Cities.
Unlocked after a Wizard Bond.
While active, both Empires may build Trade Routes to each other's Cities.
Ending the agreement cancels all Routes between the two Empires.
A Trade Route to another Empire's City grants 20% of the target City's Gold and Mana income.
Raiding
Raiding is a wartime action: it requires a declared war, plays out as a full battle against the Route's Trader Escorts, and pays out well if you win.
Raiding requires being at war with the Route's owner. Attempting to raid without a war prompts you to declare one.
Raiding a Trade Route triggers a 1v1 battle against its Trader Escorts, with no reinforcements for either side. Surviving units keep any damage they took.
A successful raid grants a one-time reward of 3× the Route's per-turn income.
Routes destroyed when a City is occupied or conquered count as raided and grant raid income.

Fixed an issue where the projectile of the Inquisitor's Shoot Crossbow and Bolt of Judgement abilities would appear from the unit's sword.
Fixed an issue where the Fire Heavy Magelock projectile was missing its muzzle flash and firing sound.
Visual Effects & Textures
Fixed an issue where the Fire Eye Happening visual would appear on unit panels and custom icon backgrounds, and adjusted its position on Monster units.
Audio
Fixed an issue where the Axe & Breachgun would be missing a firing sound when using Fire Breachgun.
Combat
Fixed an issue where unit auto-cast spells would only trigger for the first player in turn order.
Fixed an issue where Leaders summoned during combat would incorrectly count as real Leaders.
Fixed an issue where Grasping Vines would be applied for the wrong number of turns.
Fixed an issue where Astral Pull and Weaver's Retreat were incorrectly treated as Teleport abilities, subjecting them to Teleport restrictions.
Fixed an issue where Deathwaltz would not heal the target for 100% of its health.
Fixed an issue where Gravemarch, when combined with Keeper's Mark, would summon units directly instead of spawning corpses.
Fixed an issue where the turn could end while an auto combat was still being resolved.
Fixed an issue where a unit's innate damage reduction and damage channel weaknesses and resistances would not be applied in damage calculations.
Fixed an issue where unit tombstones would rise out of the ground again every time the turn changed in hotseat manual combat.
Combat Maps
Fixed an issue where the green targeting marker for corpses would sometimes not appear.
Fixed an issue where a section of stone bridge in the Umbral Tear combat map could not be walked on.
Fixed an issue where Spawn Points of Infestation would load a land battle map instead of an ocean one, or vice versa, depending on their theme or overlay.
Fixed an issue where Underground Passages would load a land battle map when placed on water overlays or themes.
Cultures
Fixed an issue where the Mystic Culture would start with 5 units instead of 4.
Fixed an issue where capturing and losing Spirit Dens would not always count toward the Primal culture quest objective. Losing a Den after the objective is completed no longer un-completes it.
Diplomacy
Fixed an issue where the Silver Tongued Society Trait would not discount the Imperium cost of House trade treaties.
Fixed an issue where House treaties would display a cost when they are free; the cost breakdown is now shown only in the tooltip.
Fixed an issue where Corrupt Pact could be cast on a Free City you are at war with.
Fixed an issue where vassal Free Cities protected by spell jammers could still be targeted with Corrupt Pact.
Fixed an issue where taking over a Free City would not cancel a Corrupt Pact cast on it by another Ruler.
Dwellings & Free Cities
Fixed an issue where relations with Free Cities and Dwellings would advance to the next diplomatic state even when progress toward that state was not allowed.
Fixed an issue where independent factions' territorial missions would target armies they were not at war with, caused by one-sided war states.
Fixed an issue where Rally of the Lieges for Dwellings would be wrongly limited by tier.
Economy
Fixed an issue where resource-sharing operations would not stop when the city being shared with was absorbed by another city.
Empire
Fixed an issue where combat summons such as Astral Reflection copies would be revivable with Unnatural Recovery after combat, allowing permanent copies of units.
Nature
Skill 10 “Druidic Empire” - Fixed an issue where it would grant +1 Knowledge, Mana and Gold per Population to Outposts; it now only affects Cities, as its description states.
Order
Skill 3 “Spiritual Conviction” - Fixed an issue where it would grant +10 Mana per City Stability above Neutral to Outposts; it now only affects Cities, as its description states.
Events
Fixed an issue where Kill Unit objectives would not complete when the target was defeated by another player.
Fixed an issue where manually spawned events belonging to a Crisis would not use the Crisis event layout.
Fixed an issue where the Umbral Dwelling's Boost Allegiance event was not linked.
Fixed an issue where the Cosmic Happenings “Asteroid” outro event would not trigger.
Fixed an issue where a Mystic Seer story event contained a grammar error.
Fixed an issue where some exploration site events (Empires & Ashes) would be missing Hero names.
Factions
Fixed an issue where the Reaver subculture would only apply to the Ruler, not their faction, for Fauster, Edward, and Valery.
Fixed an issue where mount customization options in Faction Creation were sorted incorrectly.
Fixed an issue where an Owlkin outfit had an incorrect unlock requirement.
Fixed an issue where customization item option lists could contain duplicate entries.
General

Heroes

Unit “Elder Vampire”

Fixed an issue where Siphon Blood and Draining Bite would be unusable.
Fixed an issue where Nightlord would not always be active on the Umbral Abyss and Shadow realm layers.
Fixed an issue where Vampiric Flight would have the wrong value.
Interface
Fixed an issue where some UI icons and images would fail to display after playing for a while, and icons would be shown at different zoom levels.
Fixed an issue where the number of research turns remaining would be displayed inconsistently between screens.
Fixed an issue where production queue timers for units would show the wrong number of turns.
Fixed an issue where the Outpost name prefix would appear in the wrong position.
Fixed an issue where overview map icons for Ancient Wonders from the base game, Giant Kings, and Thrones of Blood, and for the Crystal Forest, had incorrect sizes.
Fixed an issue where the Hero Customization screen would not respect visibility settings.
Fixed an issue where the Combat Preview screen would not close when another event was selected.
Fixed an issue where the Appearance settings would offer mount appearance options that are blocked for that Ruler.
Fixed an issue where the starting loadout Grimoire items had incorrect icons.
Fixed an issue where Sector Improvement tooltips would show requirement and cost elements when there are none.
Fixed an issue where the tactical combat top bar would show a dark rectangle sticking out when it expanded to fit additional resources.
Fixed an issue where the UI would not generate previews for “Target Self” abilities.
Fixed an issue where a tooltip error would occur when checking whether a relation can be boosted.
Fixed an issue where controller button glyphs would not update when switching input devices.
Fixed an issue where a map overlay was missing its color on the overview map.
Fixed an issue where the quest objective icon on the minimap would not update when the objective's target moved.
Fixed an issue where a ruined Blood Glass node would use the icon of an intact node on the overview map.
Fixed an issue where structure and district markers would render beneath domain borders.
Added a scrollbar to the House interaction buttons for when they do not all fit on screen (mainly at the largest interface scale).

Fixed an issue where combat damage previews would predict far more damage than was actually dealt. Previews no longer include the effects of damage response properties (such as Vengeful Flames) and damage reflection.
Fixed an issue where story event choices would not preview that losing allegiance would drop a Free City or Dwelling to a lower diplomatic state.
Text & Descriptions
Fixed an issue where the Teleport ability requirement had an incorrect description.
Updated the Umbral Flesh description to mention that it also affects Outposts.
Updated the Seekers of Wonders description: Outposts are included in the free annexation, but not in the extra income.
Fixed an issue where Spellblade did not mention its use of Ranged Weapons.
Fixed an issue where Large Target incorrectly stated that units were immune to displacement and knockback effects.
Fixed an issue where the Umbral Mistress's Gratitude ability description said it bypasses Defense; it now says unblockable damage.
Fixed an issue where the Goldseeker Pickaxe's Gilded effect description was missing a link to Turns and stated it lasts 1 turn instead of 2.
Removed an obsolete reference to Very Fast Movement from Advanced Logistics.
Fixed an issue where the Temple of the Exalted incorrectly stated that its governor bonus would be doubled in the city it was built in.
Fixed an issue where the Nautical Governor description did not specify Ocean and Underground water provinces.
Fixed an issue where the Watchtower City Upgrade tooltip would show wrong values.
Fixed an issue where the Healing Spires City Upgrade was missing hyperlinks and a description.
Updated the Shrouded Isle layer description to note that it cannot be terraformed.
Fixed an issue where Mana Starved's description contained a text error.
Fixed an issue where the Empire Development skill descriptions and tooltips contained multiple minor typos.
Fixed an issue where the defeat message when defeated by raiders had a plural grammar error.
Fixed an issue where the “Draft Blocked”, “Growth Blocked” and “Production Blocked” tooltips would always say “turns”, even with 1 turn remaining.
Fixed an issue where the Pall of Gloom (Umbral Disciples Society Trait, Eldritch Realms) description would be missing values.
Fixed an issue where the Tome of the Crimson Reign (Thrones of Blood) description would be cut short while researching the Tome.
Fixed an issue where the Cosmic Affinity skill tooltips would show broken text inserts.
Fixed an issue where Focus Crystal would state +10% Combat Experience in the magic material panel instead of the correct 20%.
Fixed an issue where Istarnech's heroes would have untranslated names in the Azh'ruun Pit.
Fixed various translation issues in Spanish, Korean, Polish and Russian.
Item Forge & Equipment
Fixed an issue where hero items would display the wrong damage value in the UI.
Modding
Fixed an issue where realm info would not correctly report whether a realm is modded.
Pantheon
Fixed an issue where the Conquerors and City Conquest Pantheon unlocks would trigger when migrating your own city.
Performance
Fixed an issue where opening the unit panel would be slow and its animations would start late.
Spells
Fixed an issue where the Move Portal action would take away a spell slot when cancelled; special operations not shown in the Spellbook no longer take up slots.
Fixed an issue where the Spell Discount Backfire effect would also apply to other operations.
Fixed an issue where summoning spells could still summon units onto hexes adjacent to an occupied city.
Fixed an issue where spell targeting was only cancelled when pressing Cancel; closing the spell screen in any other way now also cancels it.
Fixed an issue where World Spell “Pall of Gloom” could not be cast on Surface provinces that include Ocean, Lava, Astral Barrens or Umbral terrain hexes.
Fixed an issue where World Spell “Desecration Ritual” could not be cast on Surface provinces that include Ocean, Lava, Astral Barrens or Umbral terrain hexes.
Story Realms
Secrets of the Archmages
Fixed an issue where the Crisis of Carnage event would not reward the correct resources in Story Realm 2.
Fixed an issue in Story Realm 2 where “weekend” was written instead of “weakened”.
Thrones of Blood
Fixed an issue where certain quests in Story Realm 1 could still trigger when you were not eligible for them.
Fixed an issue where the Emperor NPC was unable to explore their starting area in Story Realm 1.
Archon Prophecy
Fixed an issue where the second Archon Prophecy Story Realm was missing its content filters.
Tomes
Astral
Tome of the Tentacle
Fixed an issue where Tendril Labyrinth would not function in water combat.
Materium
Tome of the Creator

Tome of the Golden Realm
Major Race Transformation “Goldtouched” - Fixed an issue where it would grant +1 Gold per Population to Outposts; it now only affects Cities, as its description states.
Order
Tome of Abjuration

Fixed an issue where Final Ultimatum would only restore the target's morale instead of Mind Controlling it, because the Strong Willed it applied immediately cancelled the Mind Control.
Units
Unit “War Golem” - Fixed an issue where Fiery Shift would apply Burning to allies; it now only affects enemies.
Fixed an issue where the Umbral Mistress's Wrack ability would reference a broken property.
World Map
Fixed an issue where Subjugating Raid could be exploited to repeatedly remove population from a city.
Fixed an issue where the Raiding Party siege project would grant two tiers' worth of resources when breaching the walls of a Tier 1 city.
Fixed an issue where the Gold Cursed Captain would end up in prison or on the player's side after being summoned into combat.
Fixed an issue where the Gold Cursed Captain's units would remain Undead after completing the quest.
Fixed an issue where randomly generated Marauders could have both Demonkin and Holy Aura.
Fixed an issue where diggable earth sectors would sometimes have a random uncovered hex.
Fixed an issue where diggable earth could spawn on underground water hexes, covering up Underground Passages.
Fixed an issue where players would not always start with an Underground Passage nearby.
Fixed an issue where regions containing an Underground Passage would turn into water after generation.
Fixed an issue where a province in the Breached Isles could not be annexed.

notes.title: Here is a look at what’s coming in the coming weeks

items.text: Today, we released our first hotfix addressing key issues
Next week, we will be releasing another hotfix fixing even more issues. (We’ll share more details in due time)

The week of February 24th , probably mid-week, we plan to release our first more important patch to improve optimization and our Callout Director, fixing the issues around the Callout distribution during Shifts and preventing having the two same Callouts in the same Shift.

Starting in March, we’ll probably deploy a new hotfix quickly after the release of February’s patch and will focus on a new major update planned for the middle of the month, fixing more bugs and addressing some of the feedback of the community.
Facebook Instagram TikTok Twitter
Discord Twitch Website
We are always listening closely to community feedback, but as we make any significant changes, there may be still players who have unique cases that need special care.
If even after installing all patches you are still experiencing crashes, freezes, and black screens, we need your help to find direct solutions for your problems.
Please follow this link to get us your specific details so we can investigate solutions for your case here:
