Developer Note: These changes are part of our ongoing gunplay refinement work within Battlefield Labs. Our goal is to make longer-range gunfights require players to lead their shots more consistently against moving targets, while also improving survivability for players on the receiving end. Players will now notice greater projectile travel time at range, but they will also be paired with more predictable recoil control during sustained/prolonged engagements allowing for more situations to define your scenario through skill.
Damage Multipliers

To better reward skill and mastery, average Time to Kill (TTK) has been slowed down without affecting the best possible TTK. Damage to limbs and lower torso has been reduced for all weapon classes except shotguns and sidearms.
This change generally increases the amount of shots to kill by one when hitting these areas multiple times but landing headshots will compensate for the lower damage dealt to limbs and lower torso.
In most engagements, this means that players that are more intentional about keeping their aim at the chest or at the head of their target will be more likely to win a gunfight.

To maintain weapon balance and consistency, recoil for automatic weapons has also been adjusted, headshot multipliers for automatic weapons have been slightly increased, and base damage values have received minor adjustments.
Head: Increased from 1.34x, 1.5x, 1.75x to 1.4x, 1.57x, 1.8x (depending on headshot ammo type)
Chest: Unchanged (1x) except against armor where the damage is now decreased from 1x to 0.84x
Stomach: Decreased from 1x to 0.84x
Limbs: Decreased from 1x to 0.84x
Head: Unchanged (1.34x, 1.5x, 1.75x)
Chest: Unchanged (1x) except against armor where the damage is now decreased from 1x to 0.91x
Stomach: Decreased from 1x to 0.91x
Limbs: Decreased from 1x to 0.91x
Head: Unchanged (1.75x)
Chest: Unchanged (1x) except against armor where the damage is now decreased from 0.8x to 0.67x
Stomach: Decreased from 0.8x to 0.67x
Limbs: Decreased from 0.8x to 0.67x
Weapon Dispersion

Dispersion has been adjusted to make firing behaviour more demanding for most weapons. It remains more forgiving for weapons with very low damage output, while weapons with medium to high damage output now require greater reliance on proper shooting technique and weapon mastery.

Weapons with higher damage output now experience a more aggressive increase in dispersion, especially immediately after the first shot. This places greater emphasis on burst firing or single firing when engaging at extended ranges.
Lower damage output weapons are affected less, and in some cases may have slightly reduced dispersion growth.
On average, dispersion growth has increased by 14%.
Weapons with the highest damage output can receive up to a 22% dispersion increase.
Weapons with the lowest damage output can receive up to a 48% dispersion growth reduction, with smaller differences in absolute terms.

Battlefield 6 Game Update 1.4.1.0 arrives on July 21, launching Season 4: Pacific Front and bringing naval warfare to Battlefield 6. Squads will fight across land, air, and sea with Tsuru Reef, a new large-scale Pacific battleground, marine vehicles, ocean combat, new weapons, REDSEC updates, Portal features, and more content arriving throughout the season. Take command of the coastline and turn the tide of war.
At 8:00 UTC, players will be able to download the update as it goes live across all platforms and jump in with the latest gameplay changes.

At 12:00 UTC, Season 4: Pacific Front content becomes available, with Tsuru Reef, the Dynamic Wave System, the 7.7m NSW RHIB, the RCB-90 Patrol Boat, new weapons, REDSEC updates, Portal features, new rewards, and the Season 4 Battle Pass going live.

Alongside the new content, this update also delivers a wide range of improvements across weapons, gadgets, vehicles, REDSEC, Portal, UI, audio, and overall gameplay polish to further improve the Battlefield 6 experience.
NEW CONTENT
Naval Combat & New Gameplay System

Naval Combat and New Dynamic Wave System: Naval combat has hit the harbour. Take the fight across land, sea, and air on new amphibious maps and modes, captain your crew in naval vehicles, and master the new dynamic wave system as rolling water changes movement, visibility, and engagement flow across the Pacific shoreline. Navigate hostile waters, use shifting waves to disrupt enemy sightlines, and turn the tide of war from sea to shore.
New Map

Tsuru Reef: Deploy into the biggest all-out battleground yet. Fight across a sprawling Pacific archipelago dense with luxury bungalows, tropical vegetation, jagged cliffs, and open water, with combat built around land, naval, and air warfare.
New Vehicles

RCB-90 Patrol Boat: Rule the waves in this two-seat armoured Patrol Boat built for power, pressure, and versatility. Command the coastline, push through enemy vehicles, or execute flanking manoeuvres from the water.

7.7m NSW RHIB: Joining Battlefield 6 from REDSEC, the 7.7m NSW RHIB is a fast and agile four-seat Light Transport Boat built for rapid coastal assaults. Equipped with a mounted machine gun, it gives squads a quick way to tear across the water and hit the coast.
New Weapons & Attachments

BROD 3: Aim and adapt with the BROD 3, an aggressive and versatile carbine shaped by frontline feedback. Built with a collapsible stock for maximum mobility, it’s a strong ally for squads pushing into close-range combat.
EF88: Precision meets efficiency with the EF88, a bullpup assault rifle designed for mid- to long-range combat.

VSSM: Low volume. High damage. The VSSM is a Designated Marksman Rifle with an integrated suppressor and subsonic ammunition, built for players who want to stay quiet while staying lethal. With full-auto capability, it can handle threats with both speed and stealth.

Attachments: Season 4 introduces the Extended Barrel and 1P86 LPVO sight. The Extended Barrel with a 4" extension increases projectile velocity at the cost of mobility and aim-down-sights speed, and is available for the M87A1, M1014, 18.5KS-K, and DB-12. The 1P86 LPVO provides a clear sight picture with manually switchable 1.50x and 4.50x magnification levels across supported weapons.
New REDSEC Content

Ranked Battle Royale: A new season of Ranked Battle Royale arrives with a competitive leaderboard and new permanent rewards. Squad up, climb the ranks, and drop into the deep end as naval warfare reaches the Fort Lyndon marina.
Battle Pass

Season 4 Battle Pass: Dominate every domain with new themed paths stocked with hardware, weapon packages, soldier skins, XP boosts, and more. Complete each path to unlock the final path and earn additional rewards built around command of land, air, and sea.
Battlefield Pro
Turn the tide of war with BF Pro. Gain instant BF Pro unlocks, tier skips, an exclusive bonus path, a 5% XP boost, and additional rewards designed to help you maximise progress throughout Season 4.

Water Gameplay Improvements: Water gameplay has received a broad Season 4 update, making swimming, resurfacing, Drag and Revive, underwater visibility, parachute deployment near water, and water interactions feel more consistent across combat and traversal.

European Casino map & certain content not available in REDSEC.

In case you have missed it, we are rolling out the Server Browser in Battlefield 6 early, starting with a Limited Public Scale Test launching shortly after the Casino Heist update. This stage of implementation will allow our development team to stress-test server loads, observe live queue performance, and validate matchmaking backfill with real squads.
Once this test has been completed and the necessary metrics have been verified, we will roll out the Server Browser fully to all Battlefield 6 players worldwide.
Head over to our Community Update - Server Browser Coming Soon blog to learn more.
CHANGELOG
Iron sights no longer clip into the 2.50x optic on the VCR-2.
The “To the Grave” weapon package no longer causes the soldier’s fingers to clip through its attachment.
Z84M
The pull tab now displays correctly during reload animations.
Magazines and sights no longer clip during weapon inspections when an underbarrel attachment is equipped.
The 30-Round Fast Magazine for the PW7A2 now displays a consistent description.
The 200-Round Belt Box now displays an accurate description on the L110 and M123K.
The SGX Extended Barrel now displays the correct description.
Corrected the penetration multipliers for Hollow Point, Frangible, and Tungsten Core ammunition attachments on the M121 A2.
The RSPR 5-point Muzzle Brake no longer provides greater recoil reduction than intended.
Updated the description of the Underslung Mount attachment for clarity.
Updated the layer icon for the 5-Round Fast Magazine on the Interdictor.
Resolved an issue where attachment 3D previews for the VSSM and LMR27 appeared misaligned and blurred in the Loadouts menu.
The Royal Navy Dive Knife now plays its intended first-person takedown defender animation.
Equipping the Standard Suppressor on the L115 now applies its intended hip-fire accuracy penalty.
Tungsten Core penetration ammunition on the L115 and Interdictor now applies the intended recoil values.
Corrected in-game descriptions across Low-Power Variable Optics and Thermal Sights (excluding the SU-230 and 1P86) to indicate that aiming down sights reduces movement speed
Applied the intended aim-down-sights movement speed penalty to the TH-RDS 1.00x Thermal Hybrid.
The M417 A2 25-Round Magazine attachment cost has been corrected from 15 points to 20 points.
Deploying with the 50-Round Loose Belt on the M/60 now grants the intended 250 total rounds on spawn instead of 150 rounds.
MK24
Corrected the attachment point cost for the Frangible ammunition attachment.
Magazine attachments now display the correct attachment point costs.
The bipod rail no longer appears when a handstop grip is equipped.
Resolved an issue where the Underslung Mount grenade launcher attachment was granted incorrect ammunition counts and caused a broken reload animation.
Corrected the UI icon for the Aftermarket Buffer attachment.
Weapon & Attachment Balance Updates

We have tuned several primary weapons and high-pick-rate attachments to better define their combat roles, reward deliberate shot pacing, and ensure extended magazines and specialised ammunition carry meaningful handling trade-offs.

Added a third damage drop-off step at 150m. Beyond 150m, the Mini Scout no longer deals a one-hit headshot elimination, dealing 50 damage to the chest and 33.5 damage to limbs (three hits to eliminate via limb shots).

Developer Comment: The Mini Scout features best-in-class handling, rate of fire, bullet velocity, and potential magazine capacity, alongside an innate straight-pull bolt mechanism. Combined with an infinite headshot kill distance, it rendered other sniper rifles moot, provided a player landed headshots. This adjustment preserves its dominance at close range with rapid follow-up headshots without an overly forgiving sweetspot, removing one-hit kill headshot potential beyond 150m.
Added a damage drop-off step at 55m (dealing 14.3 chest damage from 55–75m) and a new minimum damage floor of 12.76 beyond 75m.
Developer Comment: This small change helps the SCW-10 stay in its intended close-quarters lane (particularly in Battle Royale), while creating competitive breathing room for the UMG-40 and RSPR.
Increased base aim-down-sights speed by one tier to match the submachine gun baseline.
Factory and Light Barrels now grant hip-fire accuracy improvements instead of aim-down-sights speed bonuses.
Extended Barrel now grants recoil reduction at the cost of an aim-down-sights speed penalty.

Developer Comment: The GRT-BC was increasingly overshadowed by the BROD 3. These adjustments give the platform a distinct combat role bridging Carbines and Submachine Guns, leveraging its compact bullpup profile for innate aim-down-sights speed, while allowing the extended barrel handguard to add stabilising front-end weight for better recoil control.
Increased deploy time index by one step to align with the RPKM and RPK-74M.
60-Round Drum (Regular): + Draw Speed.
60-Round Fast Drum: + Aim-Down-Sights Move Dispersion.
45-Round Compact (Compact 1): -25% Capacity, +Aim-Down-Sights Speed, +Draw Speed, +Sway, +Aim-Down-Sights Moving Dispersion.
50-Round Compact (Compact 2): -17% Capacity, +Draw Speed, +Sway, +Aim-Down-Sights Moving Dispersion.
45-Round Fast Magazine (Compact 3): -25% Capacity, +Aim-Down-Sights Speed, +Draw Speed, +Sway, +Aim-Down-Sights Moving Dispersion, +Reload Speed.

Developer Comment: Re-establishes the KTS100 MK8 as a steady, methodical squad support platform. Magazines that previously granted a +20% reload speed benefit have been adjusted to ensure tangible vulnerability between reloads. Dialling back the handling attributes of the KTS100 MK8 helps in preventing the weapon from functioning as an oversized assault rifle, opening strategic space for the SOR-556 Mk2.
KV9 & SCW-10 Extended Magazine 1 now applies a weapon draw speed penalty, and Extended Magazine 2 now applies both aim-down-sights speed and weapon draw speed penalties.
SG 553R Extended Magazine 1 and 2 now apply a weapon draw speed penalty, and Fast Extended Magazine 2 now applies a weapon draw speed penalty and a reduced reload speed bonus.

Developer Comment: These extended magazines saw roughly 80% pick rates, heavily skewing weapon viability. Players routinely sacrificed customisation points to bypass the natural trade-offs of close-range dominance. Penalising handling and draw times ensures players sprinting into combat unprepared cannot instantly snap to target, reducing effective time-to-kill advantages and encouraging standard or quick-reload magazine choices.
Match Grade Ammunition aerodynamic drag coefficient increased from 0.0002 to 0.00025.
Removed Synthetic Tip Ammunition from the DRS-IAR.

Developer comment: The DRS-IAR is arguably the most versatile weapon in BF6 with high RoF and great LMG dispersion + recoil. By selecting moderate attachments in other categories, Synthetic Tip ammo was a no-brainer, pushing its effectiveness over the edge.
Frangible Ammunition customisation point cost reduced from 20 to 15 points across all weapons.
Reduced the recoil reduction effectiveness of the Aftermarket Buffer attachment.
Added a reload speed bonus to the Magwell Flare alongside its aim-down-sights reload capability.
Underslung Mount customisation point cost reduced from 10 to 5 points across all compatible weapons.
Iron Sights customisation point cost reduced from 15 to 10 points across all Sniper Rifles.
The Gunslinger attachment on the M44 now grants hip-fire accuracy improvements instead of draw speed.

Updated the SV-98 Flash Compensator to use Flash Hider characteristics (suppressing 2D minimap spotting only) and the SV-98 Suppressor to use standard Suppressor characteristics (suppressing both 2D minimap and 3D in-world spotting).

Developer comment: The SV-98 has limited muzzle options, so by shuffling the effects and costs of the existing muzzles the weapon will now have a greater variety of builds with the ability to hide 2D spot-on-fire.
First-person hand animations now play correctly after interacting with a door while holding a melee weapon.
Removed the mirrored Battlefield logo from the right glove of the “Red Ghost Saboteur” character skin.
Resolved flickering on the wrist device on the “Death Knell” character skin.
Uniform patches now display correctly on the “Vortex” character skin.
Resolved mask clipping on the “Controlled Burn” character skin.
Corrected a typo on the “Rampant Raze” helmet patch.
Resolved a texture issue on the “Highest Roller” character skin.
Resolved an issue where the guided missile was unresponsive when fired from the WSO seat in the multirole jet.
Vehicles now launch into the air less often when colliding with other vehicles.
Heavy Warheads now increase the ammunition count of Aim-Guided Rockets on the Panthera KHT Attack Helicopter.
RCB-90
The mortar now displays accurate distance information.
The mortar turret now displays correctly when the “Typhoon Rider” skin is equipped.
Resolved an issue that could cause helicopters to launch into the air when hit by a Support Supply Bag.
Resolved an issue where thrown Supply Pouches did not lock onto friendly players as intended.
Several gadget and melee weapon skins now appear correctly in-game when equipped.
Helicopters no longer flip abruptly when a passenger throws a Supply Pouch. You thought you were flippin’.
Corrected an issue where the Supply Pouch ammunition count could become inconsistent after resupplying from a Supply Crate.
The Handheld Jammer can only be self-applied, removing the option to deploy on the ground.
Added Rush, Team Deathmatch, and Domination to Vegas Strip.
Added the Casino Heist addition M142 MRAS to existing Conquest layouts:
Area 51 (Conquest): Replaced one Main Battle Tank at each team’s HQ with an M142 MRAS.
Railway to Golmud (Conquest): Replaced the Mobile Anti-Air at Objective B with an M142 MRAS, and replaced the Main Battle Tank at Objective A with an Infantry Fighting Vehicle.
Operation Firestorm (Conquest): Replaced one Main Battle Tank at each team’s HQ with an M142 MRAS.
Mirak Valley (Conquest): Added one M142 MRAS to each team’s HQ.
Extended the idle timeout by 90 seconds in Operations, Breakthrough, Carrier Strike, Conquest, and Escalation.
Resolved an issue causing the restricted area UI to appear too early on blocked stationary weapon spawners.
Out-of-bounds notifications no longer appear too early when blocking vehicle spawners, and the notification message now more clearly explains the restriction.
Resolved a lighting issue that could cause overly bright spots to appear across maps.
Resolved multiple progression tracking and criteria issues across Season 5 Weekly Challenges.
Fixed an issue where the Week 8 Bonus Challenge failed to track player redeploys while playing in REDSEC game modes.
Resolved a discrepancy where in-game requirements for the Week 9 Challenge did not match the completion criteria displayed and tracked.
Fixed a progression calculation bug with the Week 7 Bonus Challenge in Rapid Royale matches.
Corrected tracking behavior for the Week 4 Bonus Challenge so that Multiplayer and REDSEC-specific progression criteria now track independently as intended, rather than advancing simultaneously.
Updated the Week 10 Challenge description to accurately reflect that Superior items collected across all Royale modes (including Rapid Royale) count toward progress.
Resolved a progression calculation bug with the Week 9 Challenge in standard Battle Royale modes.
Fixed a progression calculation bug with the Week 9 Challenge in Rapid Royale matches.
Updated the Week 8 Challenge criteria and tracking to correctly monitor top squad placements across all supported Royale modes.
Fixed a progression calculation bug with the Week 7 Challenge in standard Battle Royale matches.
Weapon icons now update correctly in the soldier inventory HUD when switching weapons as the Assault class.
Resolved an issue where squad orders could trigger unintentionally when cancelling out of the objective list in the Commo Rose.
The gadget slot replenish animation no longer plays when performing a melee attack.
Resolved an issue where 100 lethal damage could display as 99 damage next to the crosshair under certain circumstances.
Victory Squad names and the Winner banner no longer overlap on the End of Round cinematic screen.
Adjusted the Squad Leader icon to display at its intended size.
Resolved texture corruption around the outer boundaries of the Big Map across multiple maps, including Wake Island and Manhattan Bridge.
Corrected Canted Iron Sight and PAS-35 Thermal optic alignment on layered weapon icons across the VCR-2, NVO-228E, SGX, AK-205, Kord 6P67, RSPR, and L115.
The Picture-in-Picture camera no longer refreshes unnecessarily when closing the scoreboard.
Vehicle icons on objectives now fade out as intended when pinned to the screen edge on the Deploy Screen.
Restored missing icons in the vehicle deploy list on the Deploy Screen.
Objective B on Railway to Golmud now displays the M142 MRAS icon instead of the Main Battle Tank icon in the vehicle availability UI.
The pre-match briefing screen on Vegas Strip no longer displays only the underground area if the previous match ended while underground.
Removed unnecessary AI disconnect and reconnect notifications from the HUD.
The redeploy camera preview no longer overlaps vehicle icons when viewing the NATO HQ on the Deploy Screen on Vegas Strip.
Exiting the weapon customisation menu in a pre-round lobby no longer opens the Mission Briefing screen.
Improved the text for inactivity kick and leave penalty notifications.
Resolved several UI and navigation issues with Shortcut Kits in the Store, improving menu functionality, readability, and presentation.
Resolved an issue that prevented players from returning to the lobby or closing the “Quit Game” pop-up as expected.
Underbarrel attachments now remain visible on weapons when entering the Firing Range.
Resolved a text overlap issue on the Task Force Sparhawk Unit Details screen in Loadouts.
Improved the readability of the “Start” text on the Custom Search tile.
Realigned attachment indicator lines across several weapons in the Loadouts menu for improved accuracy.
Corrected a typo in the “Distance traveled with Parachute” statistic in the Player Profile.
The Event tab now highlights the featured reward tile as intended after exiting the Event takeover screen.
Resolved an animation issue affecting 3D soldier models when navigating between the Profile and Settings menus.
Resolved camera positioning issues that could cause weapons to appear off-centre in the Weapon Customisation menu.
Patrol Boats no longer clip into the ground on the Vehicle Customisation inspection screen after visiting the Deploy Screen.
Corrected a colour inconsistency on the “Dry Spell” Spray icon.
Losing network connectivity while in the Firing Range no longer causes the game to become unresponsive.
Resolved visual alignment issues affecting soldiers and weapons in the Loadouts menu and pre-game lobby.
The Player Profile now displays the accurate total Dog Tags count.
Owned items no longer cause Mastery information to overlap in the Shortcut Kits bundle preview on PlayStation 5.
Pressing Esc to dismiss menu pop-ups in the main menu no longer opens the “Quit Game” pop-up.
Custom weapon packages for unowned weapons now appear without delay in the Loadouts menu after being purchased in a Store bundle.
Corrected the spelling of Dev Kulkarni’s name in the biography for Mantra (Steel Talon)
Hardware Challenge rewards now display their proper player-facing names instead of internal dev names.
Resolved a crash that could occur when the minimap attempted to render at an unsupported size.
Pressing ESC after changing Display or Graphics settings now triggers the confirmation prompt as expected.
Changing the Neutral Colour in Colour Profiles no longer affects the scrollbar in Vehicle Customisation.
Game settings no longer reset to default after an unexpected PC shutdown.
Resolved an issue where a game update could reset player settings and display a save file corruption error.
Players no longer clip through terrain at the edges of Portal maps.
Deleting a parent UI widget in Portal now also deletes its child widgets, preventing a server crash.
The Commo Rose now displays text and images correctly across all Portal maps.
Added Convergence Event assets and visual effects to Underground, Area 51, and Sandbox in Portal.

Added White Balance, Vignette, Tone Map, Motion Blur, Fog, Filmic Effects, Film Grain, Depth of Field, Unitology Glyphs, and Colour Correction to Portal’s ScreenEffects selection list, along with the SetScreenEffectParameter action to customise screen effect parameters.

Added seven new entries to the SoldierEffects selection list: two visual effects (ShadowSilhouette and NecromorphEffects) and five local audio effects (HearDroneLoop, HearWhispers, HearFakeFootstepsAndGunshots, HearFakeMonsterNoises, and HearFakeMonsterNoises2).
Portal creators can now select class-specific skin variations—including the Marked Soldier appearance—when spawning Custom Portal Bots with SpawnAIFromAISpawner.
The M142 MRAS vehicle is now available in Portal.
Added Area 51 and Vegas Strip support to Portal.
Added BitFlag function nodes for managing variables and added support for customising Physics Raycast hit layers in Portal.
Added WaterPlane support to the Portal SDK.
The scoreboard no longer appears empty after transitioning to the next match in Portal.
Custom Lobbies & Spectator Mode
The “Player Actions” button can now be selected in Portal Custom Lobbies.
The “No Host” notification no longer appears unintentionally when leaving a Portal Custom Lobby.
The “Enable Lobby” option is now available when hosting Battle Royale Duos and King of the Hill in Portal Custom Lobbies.
Corrected a typo in the “Join As Party” host setting description in Portal Custom Lobbies.
Conquest loading screens in Portal Custom Lobbies now display the correct map images for the selected maps.
Admins no longer remain listed in the banned players list after receiving a “Ban Failed” error message in Portal Custom Lobbies.
Resolved an issue in Spectator Mode on Cairo Bazaar where the free camera could become stuck on invisible geometry.
Player inventories no longer appear empty after switching between first-person and third-person views in Custom Lobby Spectator Mode.
Spectators can now switch from the current player to other players while in first-person view using the assigned keybind.
The Spectator soldier HUD no longer disappears after rejoining a match through the reconnect feature.
Resolved an issue where the Spectator Big Map cursor did not align with or select the intended player at certain screen resolutions.
Resolved an issue where the Spectator UI could appear too early or remain on screen too late.
Switching rapidly between players in first-person view in Custom Lobby Spectator Mode no longer causes soldier geometry to flash.
Switching between free camera and follow camera while spectating in Portal Battle Royale no longer briefly shows a skymap camera or clips into a stationary spectated soldier’s head.
The Z84M no longer sounds as though it fires extra shots when heard at a distance.
Resolved an issue where the Commo Rose UI indicator for the active vehicle radio station could be missing, and added missing radio stations to the vehicle Commo Rose.
Vehicle tyre and track audio now transitions smoothly across different surface materials on Vegas Strip.
The L115 now plays its bolt-action sound effect correctly when reloading from an empty magazine.
Resolved an issue where a loud sonar-like sound could play near Objective E on Wake Island in Conquest.
Commander voice-over lines now trigger reliably when remaining reinforcements drop to 50 and 25 in Rush.
Commander voice-over lines now play as intended after capturing an objective in Domination.
Commander voice-over lines now trigger when either team reaches a 20% lead in Domination.
REDSEC
Resolved an issue where Redeploy Tokens did not spawn in ambulances during Rapid Royale Solos.
Resolved an issue where loot chests could close if opened at the exact moment chests reset in Battle Royale, or appear empty the first time they were opened in Rapid Royale.
Upgrade Kits no longer spawn upside down inside Rapid Royale Ordnance Drop crates.
Secondary weapon cards now consistently update their rarity colour when using an Upgrade Kit in Battle Royale without requiring players to swap weapons first.
Resolved an issue where Upgrade Kits could display UI for and upgrade the wrong weapon.
Support players no longer receive Assault Upgrade Kits from Class Armory Crates in Rapid Royale Solos.
Armor Plates now automatically pick up as intended in Battle Royale.
Sabotage blood splatter visual effects now remain visible for the full duration a player takes damage inside a sabotaged vehicle.
Added Recommended Zones for human squads in Casual Battle Royale, awarding bonus XP upon landing at the assigned zone.
Added Battle Pickups to Superior Weapon Mission Rewards in Battle Royale.
Soldiers no longer appear misoriented in the back of the helicopter during the Battle Royale and Rapid Royale insertion sequence.
Phantom Program mission items now drop as intended when the carrier is eliminated or disconnects.
Winning a Battle Royale match while a teammate redeploy beacon triggers no longer causes the redeploy animation to play over the extraction sequence or result in a softlock.
Resolved an issue where a Battle Royale match would not end if the Phantom Program team failed the mission but won by elimination.
The bomb in the Battle Royale Wreckage mission now deals environmental damage when its fuse expires and downs any player holding it.
Moved Phantom Program mission objects from the USS Grant to the Walker-Senex Campus.
Acquiring a Phantom Program Fragment now shares challenge progress with the entire squad rather than only the player who picked it up.
Selecting a mission in Battle Royale no longer causes the player to jump.
Added an overtime condition for the Weapons Cache mission in Battle Royale when a player is actively opening the cache as the timer expires.

Removed automatic squad-wipe completion for the countering team in the Battle Royale Decryption/Interception mission; if the original team is wiped, the countering team must still decrypt the beacon to complete the mission.
Resolved an issue in Rapid Royale on Vegas Strip where players could land on an out-of-bounds roof and become trapped.
The final mission cinematic for the Phantom Program now plays with its intended audio and sound effects.
Items on the roof of the Olympus lobby on Vegas Strip no longer sink slightly into the roof and can now be picked up as intended.
The Signal Hack antenna alignment position can now be reached as intended in Battle Royale.
Resolved multiple locations where loot crates or items failed to spawn in Rapid Royale across Mirak Valley and Vegas Strip.
The insertion sequence in Battle Royale and Rapid Royale is no longer obscured by a black blur effect.
Resolved an issue where the Rapid Royale pre-game lobby appeared overexposed.
Smoke Grenade Launchers no longer fire High Explosive grenades when equipped by Assault players in Battle Royale after reaching the third Field Upgrade level.
Players can no longer inadvertently pick up deployed Supply Crates in Rapid Royale.
Added the Signal Jammer to the Battle Royale loot pool.
Resolved an issue where an incorrect camo was applied to the Z84M when looted at or upgraded to Advanced rarity in Battle Royale.
The Anti-Vehicle Gear Drop and Explosive Ordnance Transporter no longer display a blank icon when a nearby tank threatens them.
Players can now see their available Armor Plates and upgrades when HUD input prompts are turned off.
The “Eliminated” UI message no longer displays twice when a player bleeds out and redeploys in Battle Royale.
The Victory UI is no longer delayed after winning a round in Battle Royale and Rapid Royale.
The beacon calibration UI in the Battle Royale Decryption/Interception mission now disappears as intended when the mission is completed.
Ordnance Drop icons in Rapid Royale now turn yellow as intended after landing.

Added an in-world icon for the Battle Royale Decryption/Interception mission when a player moves too quickly with the beacon, and resolved an issue where grounded beacons appeared owned by both allies and enemies.
Removed several “Squad” text references from the End of Round screen and HUD in Rapid Royale Solos.
Reduced the size of in-world Point of Interest labels in Rapid Royale.
Added new Mission Menu icons for the Wreckage and Marked missions in Battle Royale.
Added a survival timer to the HUD widget for tank drivers targeted by the Tank Hunter mission in Battle Royale.
Spectators can now see the Redeploy Token UI in Rapid Royale.
Resolved inconsistent ping indicators for Ordnance Drops on the Big Map and minimap in Rapid Royale.
Improved the visuals of the Redeploy Token HUD elements in Rapid Royale.
The Phantom Program mission area entrance notification no longer displays repeatedly after entering and exiting the mission area multiple times.
The Big Map no longer opens overly zoomed out in Rapid Royale on Vegas Strip.
Players using a controller can now navigate the Pause Menu with the left stick while spectating a teammate in Battle Royale.
Redeploy Token icons now replenish in the intended order when obtaining a new token in Rapid Royale.
Synchronised the Data Extraction sequence sound effects with its animation in Battle Royale.
Redeploy Token voice-over lines no longer continue to trigger after Redeploy Tokens are disabled in Rapid Royale Trios.
The Handler now plays the intended voice-over lines when starting an Evasion mission in Battle Royale.
The Handler voice-over line notifying players that Redeploy Tokens are disabled now plays as intended in Rapid Royale.
The “Threat Avoided” voice-over line no longer plays erroneously upon completing a mission in Battle Royale.
The Ranked Battle Royale “Rules & Points” page now displays the correct kill and assist caps for 21st–25th placements.
Seasons now appear in chronological order in the Ranked Leaderboard season filter.

For the latest updates, keep an eye on Steam Discussions and our BattlefieldComm X account. If you need to report any issues, please visit EA forums. If you want to take part in Q&As, giveaways, community events, or find a squad, join the Battlefield Discord.

items.text: Greetings Sinners!

Many of you are eagerly awaiting the Balance and True Torment Patch and we're happy to confirm that this next update for the Mea Culpa expansion will release for Steam on Tuesday, 3rd December. We want to ensure that the update is as high quality as possible on release.
Following this release our focus will shift towards bringing all updates to Epic, GoG and Console versions of Blasphemous 2.
The Game Kitchen & Team17
We have released an update patch on STEAM today to resolve unexpected issues such as crashes that have been occurring.
Resolved crashes occurring during Story Mode.
Fixed crashes when selecting modes from the menu or returning to the menu from various modes.
Addressed crashes occurring at the start or end of online matches.
Improved overall stability related to loading processes.
Fixed an issue where the application would crash when switching the application to inactive by pressing Alt+Tab in Fullscreen Mode.
Fixed an issue where the screen would freeze if the application window is continuously moved during the loading screen in Window Mode.

We have confirmed that this update resolves some of the issues. However, if you continue to experience problems, we will prioritize investigation and address them promptly. Should you encounter any crashes or unexpected behaviors, please kindly provide your feedback in the comments of this thread.
Additionally, it would be greatly appreciated if you could provide the following information to help us improve our support:
GPU
CPU
OS (e.g., Windows 10, Windows 11 HOME, Windows 11 PRO)
OS version
Graphics mode (Quality mode, Balanced mode, Performance mode)
Window mode (Windowed, Borderless Window, Fullscreen)
Game language
PC's regional settings/language
Details of the issue

Additionally, if a crash report file is generated during a crash, we would be grateful if you could send it to Bandai Namco Customer Support along with the above information. Please do not post these files in this thread.
C:/Users/YourUsername/AppData/Local/CrashDumps
Filename: BLEACH_Rebirth_of_Souls.exe.●●●●.dmp
Bandai Namco Customer Support: https://bnfaq.channel.or.jp/inquiry/3177
*This contact is for Japanese support only. For international inquiries, please contact us through the following link:
We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding and cooperation.

We've been listening to the community since launch and have seen the comments about optimization and performance. We take this seriously, and want to take a moment and talk about the strides and advancements we’ve made.

A lot of our optimization work for PC players has centered on providing meaningful improvements in frame rate without noticeable sacrifices to the game, including visual fidelity, that are fundamental to the artistic intent of Gearbox’s developers. Our primary objective is to strike the balance between making sure players can notice the frame rate improvements we’re making without disrupting their experience.
Over the past several months, these optimizations have improved average FPS by approximately 20% across the board, including on our minimum and recommended specifications.
But this is just the start. We've also greatly improved stability, reducing the amount of crashes affecting players.
We know we have work left to do, and we're continuing to optimize for the future. So let's talk about some of the ways we've improved PC Performance on Borderlands 4 since launch.
[dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l656gL0nv0c"]
Let's take a look at how performance at launch compares to our upcoming March 26 patch for Mad Ellie and the Vault of the Damned:
(Warning: this is about to get highly technical, but the key takeaway is the ~20% gain in average frame rates across different PC specs.)

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157740/3a763c0b6836a7eac4c2b1a39a9daccfa551280d.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157740/fc41bbbf989253ffc8d89e60ff1ad99ca2fc46f3.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45157740/3d5856b02038b1fb8fc66feb3fa7c3d9c49e928c.png"]

The roughly 20% increase in average FPS comes from combined efforts focusing on GPU, CPU, and general efficiency, with the Optimization Team identifying specific refinements to improve performance without being too noticeable in terms of visual fidelity.

In addition to improving average FPS, we reduced stutters, improving the 1% and 0.1% lows in frame rate. These are the bottom 1% and 0.1% of frames generated during our benchmark test and are indicators of frame stability. The closer these numbers are to the average FPS, the smoother and more responsive the game will feel, reducing stutters and hitches.

Hitching is among the top challenges impacting performance, as a stuttering frame rate can really take you out of the action. We reduced hitching by refining our PSO (Pipeline State Objects) process to avoid overloading the game system with too many effects.

Shader PSOs exist to make rendering faster by having the graphics drivers generate a final optimal shader for a specific GPU in specific conditions. However, the tradeoff is that those drivers need time to generate the shaders when encountering them for the first time, leading to hitches. Developers usually solve this by pre-building shaders before entering a level or letting the system build them in the background; we do both.

Borderlands 4 is known for having billions of guns, each one dynamically spawned with dedicated materials for each part. It's a great recipe for fun, but a challenging task for the team's rendering programmers. Since launch, we improved the way Borderlands 4 enables your graphics drivers early detection of new material on special effects and weapons, therefore ensuring these drivers are ready.

Another big area of optimization is our HLOD (Hierarchical Level of Detail) that renders areas of the map that are farther off in the distance. We reworked how the low-detail mesh looks in a way that's hopefully imperceptible, so you don't notice any change when traversing the seamless world of Kairos without any loading screens.

Lastly, we greatly improved stability since launch, reducing how often players encounter crashes. And since December alone, we’ve nearly halved the crash rate, from 0.63% of all sessions to 0.38% (and 17% of players experiencing a crash down to 9.35%).

When it comes to visual effects, we found ways to reduce your GPU's workload by trimming polygon counts for certain effects like thruster exhausts, Action Skill particle effects, and Airship drop world events, just to name a few examples.

Likewise, we lessened strain on CPUs by refining things like Cryo damage effects, collision physics, and cloth simulation. There may be times on Kairos when you're seeing all of these effects and more at once, so the GPU and CPU optimizations go a long way!

We also made headway in lighting across Kairos, using the Virtual Shadow Maps technology of Unreal 5 to improve performance. Borderlands 4 introduced dynamic time-of-day lighting across day and night cycles, meaning that every frame has to account for the sun's position. That leads to a ton of per-frame calculations, which we're now able to cache using Virtual Shadow Maps to reduce the load on your GPU. We also did some fine-tuning with better lighting shaders and skylight environment map updates.

Lastly (for today's discussion at least), we made backend code improvements to greatly improve UI efficiency. You shouldn't notice a difference when perusing your ECHO Menus or delighting in the damage numbers hovering above wounded enemies, but rest assured that they're working better than ever when it comes to performance.
We're proud of the work the team's done to improve Borderlands 4's PC performance since launch, and we also recognize we have more to do. We’re in it for the long haul!

We are doing all of this without removing the ability that players have had, and will continue to have, to self-tune their experiences to fit their playstyle preferences using the in-game graphics options and graphics card-based drivers and tools.

Thanks again for your support and patience, and an extra special thanks to everyone who submitted feedback. Every ticket sent to 2K Support helps us identify, track, and diagnose problems so we can make more refinements; please don't hesitate to reach out if you're encountering any issues.
As always, we'll continue listening to every piece of feedback and finding more ways to improve your experience. We're honored to have you with us on Kairos, Vault Hunter.

releases.displayName: GAME DIFFICULTY & PLAYER FREEDOM UPDATE INCOMING!

items.text: Hey everyone!
The development team here at Spitfire has been working feverishly over the past several weeks, and is excited to deliver the Game Difficulty and Player Freedom update very soon.

We've developed two new difficulty modes to help players find the right balance for their tastes. A range of missions, including Home Target and Heard on the News have had significant balancing adjustments that should help players complete them more intuitively.

To make the game more approachable for a range of play styles, and allow players to feel more in control, we've removed most hero-specific optional objectives and re-tuned optional objective requirements across many missions. Additionally, some SP will be awarded for completing missions regardless of optional objectives. A new gameplay setting optionally moves the All In One Bonus SP reward to mission completion for players who don't enjoy trying to fulfil all objectives at once. Together, we hope these changes will make the game more approachable and comfortable for players who feel Capes is too “puzzle-like”.

For players who have been enjoying Capes in its current state, we have worked to preserve the game as you know it in the Challenging difficulty mode (formerly "Normal" difficulty) while also bringing in level-specific balancing improvements.

In addition to these changes, we’ve made a number of quality of life improvements. To speed up gameplay, we’ve updated fast forward to work during players’ turns (incl. Ultimates!). Initiative values have been added to the Turn Order when previewing abilities that affect Initiative to more clearly indicate what is happening. Also, for achievement hunters and those players chasing Hero Challenges, we’ve made the active team’s Challenges list available from the Pause menu during combat.
This is just a taster of the changes coming in the Game Difficulty and Player Freedom update, and we look forward to sharing it with you all on the 28th of June.
Spitfire Interactive
Some in-progress missions will be reset when the update drops. Affected missions include:
Act I
Mugging
Which Way the Wind Blows
Double Damage
Act II
Tech Support
Rooftop Hostage
City Surveillance
Streets of Rage
Industrial Sabotage
Act III
Primax (Boss)

Knights,

The Reclamation Update (2.9) will be in your hands tomorrow, November 7. Chivalry 2 players will get to dive into the huge new Team Objective map The Reclamation of Montcrux, try out the new Siege Crossbow, and play new limited time game mode types, along with improvements to combat and quality of life.
With update 2.9, the Royal Zweihander and Steam loyalty helmets will be made available for all. 250 Crowns will also be gifted for free to all players over the next week.

We’re also excited to be bringing additional content updates to Chivalry 2 in 2024. One Team Objective map that we’re working on is an incredible one, set to deliver one of the most memorable gaming moments in Chivalry franchise history.
Stay tuned for more updates to Chivalry 2’s public roadmap.

While we’re pleased to be working on exciting new content and features for the game still to come, we do have some news to share today: cross-progression between Epic Games Store and Steam player profiles will not be implemented in Chivalry 2.
We had previously said this feature would be coming in mid-late 2022, and much time has passed since then.

Overall, we underestimated the full development cost for this feature. It would have eaten up considerable development time that, throughout 2022 and 2023, would have meant a much slower cadence of new game updates to Chivalry 2 (and would have continued to do so into the future). We had made some steps towards its implementation when we first spoke about the feature, but paused development on it in 2022 while we took further time to gauge its full development cost.

There are other upcoming features consuming significant development time that we still aim to deliver to Chivalry 2 that we know will serve a much wider variety of players, much like Crossplay Parties did, which we delivered with update 2.8.

We understand that many players will be disappointed by this news. This is not an announcement we had wanted to make either, but it is our hope that this message provides some transparency on our decision not to implement cross-progression.
Seeing the high number of community requests we have decided that alongside the Reclamation Update (2.9) we will be releasing the following cosmetics for all users on all platforms:
The Royal Zweihander, previously a pre-order exclusive, is now purchasable for 2000 gold
The Steam Loyalty Helmets are now available for all platforms for 1 gold

We know that many players on Epic, Steam and console platforms wanted to ensure they could access these cosmetics on their platform of choice - so we hope this provides a fair means to accessing the content in the absence of cross-progression.
Players can also enjoy some of Chivalry 2’s purchasable cosmetics with the 250 Crown gift we’ll be granting to all accounts over the course of this week.
After the Reclamation update, Chivalry 2 players can look forward to yet another content update in the new year - the work for which is all very much underway!
Stay tuned for more details about this update.
Our support and love for Chivalry will continue, and we look forward to joining you all on more battlefields along the way.
Onward, to glory!

The Company of Heroes 3: 3.0 Update arrives as part of the 20th Anniversary celebrations for the Company of Heroes franchise. Our biggest update to Company of Heroes 3 since launch, 3.0 delivers major improvements across the core game experience, including environments and visuals, effects, audio, A.I., gameplay, maps, campaigns, balance, and more.

New weather effects, seasonal environments, lighting and visual improvements bring greater variety and atmosphere to the battlefield, while a collection of new and refreshed maps, campaign improvements, and quality-of-life updates further refine the Company of Heroes 3 experience.
Update 3.0 introduces a substantial visual and environmental overhaul across Company of Heroes 3, bringing greater variety, atmosphere, and battlefield readability to maps throughout the game.
New winter, autumn and industrial environments
Snow and rain weather effects
Dynamic terrain wetness, transitioning between dry and wet conditions
Enhanced soldier lighting for improved readability
Improved atmospheric fog, smoke, and environmental effects
Improved bloom and emissive effects
Additional map and environmental visual improvements
The sights and sounds of the battlefield are also receiving a significant update in 3.0, with improvements to combat audio and visual effects alongside an expanded selection of music.
Improved weapon firing sounds
Enhanced impact and explosion audio
Improved vehicle destruction audio
Expanded music selection featuring classic tracks from Company of Heroes and Company of Heroes 2

Final Stand is receiving a large content update that focuses on improving replayability. We are adding co-op for up to 3-players, a new Battleground, additional unit unlocks, new passive technologies, and new ability unlocks.
In 3-player co-op, enemy events will scale up in magnitude based on player count.
There will be buffs for players and a few new tricks for the enemy.
Update 3.0 brings a collection of new and refreshed maps to Company of Heroes 3, alongside broader improvements to map visuals and environments.

US Forces – Climb to Glory
Wehrmacht – Edelweiss
British Forces – Bloody Baltic
Deutsches Afrikakorps – Cold Snap
Victory Point – Industrial
Update 3.0 includes a wide-ranging pass on the Company of Heroes 3 campaign experience, addressing longstanding issues while improving campaign presentation, clarity, and gameplay.

New clear neutral lighting for better readability - improved readability on the Campaign map by reducing the noise of unimportant items such as farmland, railroad tracks and road variations, and increasing the contrast and readability of important landmarks such as cities, hospitals, ports, etc.
Revisited lighting, dressing and atmosphere on all Campaign missions to modify the tone to be more dramatic and to make it more varied and authentic than before
Certain costlier sections of the Campaign map have been optimized

In Update 3.0, we are improving team games with a focus on making tactics and positioning more important throughout Company of Heroes 3. You can find the full list of changes in the incoming patch notes, but for a quick overview:
Multiplayer has undergone targeted changes to improve the feel of larger team games
Major Economy Rework
Rebalance of Artillery
Reduction of massing vehicles
Stronger Emphasis on Positioning
Reworked an existing Battlegroup and made several small adjustments to others
Improved A.I logic for Combat Assessment
U.I Elements tidied up to convey critical gameplay information
Improved how possible matches are evaluated in multiplayer modes during matchmaking

The biggest change will be the way the A.I. calculates unit strength so it can judge fights more realistically and make better decisions when assessing what to build in what order. We will cover these in more depth in the patch notes.

Update 3.0 will also introduce a substantial balance pass, with changes across factions, units, abilities, and the wider multiplayer experience. For a full list of all incoming balance changes, be sure to check out our patch notes.
Tune in to our fireside chat on November 5th on our Company of Heroes Twitch channel for more.
From the Rangers, to the Whizbang, to the Bersaglieri, our incoming global balance changes range across multiple units and systems to improve the general multiplayer experience.
Overall game pacing, economy, and resources

Increasing the versatility of late game Wehrmacht

items.text: Being able to customize the look of your factions in Company of Heroes 3 has proven to be very popular with our players, and we have heard a lot of feedback requesting additional unit and profile cosmetics, more frequent releases of cosmetic sets, and general store and loadout improvements. With the Topaz Rhino (2.3.0) update releasing on March 31st, we will be implementing a lot of these changes, and laying the groundwork to do more in the future. This work will run in tandem with our future content plans for additional Battlegroups and gameplay content, as we have a lot more to share in the months ahead!

The Topaz Rhino update includes a major revamp of the in-game store and our cosmetic sets. This will include a fresh, new look to streamline the management of your cosmetic loadout, and improvements to make navigating, purchasing, and equipping items in the store a lot more straightforward. Our new cosmetics showcase allows you to preview cosmetics, rotate the camera, and really get a great sense for how they actually look in game. We plan to show these changes in more detail in our Deep Dive livestream next week, but here you can get a sneak peek of the work in progress! Additionally, we’ll be granting certain cosmetics for eligible players (more details below) when that update goes live at the end of the month.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40883127/3913eebf7b2db734dcae823c54abe19681178357.png"]A pre-release version of our new store and showcase mode.
Today we will cover several different, but related topics we aim to improve with this next update:
Cosmetic sets broken up into smaller bundles
Finishing “incomplete” cosmetic sets
Granting all cosmetic items in a set – even if you own some, but not all of them
How changing the Hammer & Shield pack affects players who only own one of the included Battlegroups
New item types in the store

Cosmetic sets will no longer be broken into smaller bundles. Moving forward, cosmetics will only be available as a complete or Ultimate Set. We found that players were often frustrated by which units were (or were not) included in bundles, and it often made collecting a complete set confusing.

Today we are delisting all smaller bundles and individual cosmetic items from the in-game store. On March 31st, these cosmetics will be available in their Ultimate Set. As an example, the Sea Blue M8 Greyhound Armored Car cosmetic for the US Forces can no longer be purchased individually – it will only be available in the Sea Blue Ultimate Set.

The only exceptions to this will be the Night Fighters cosmetic items, which will still be available individually for now, and the Devil’s Brigade cosmetics which were only available as a pre-order bonus.

Previously, we had a few cosmetic sets that only included some of a faction’s base unit roster, but not all of them, such as the Nature’s Vanguard set for the British Forces which only included vehicles. These sets will now include cosmetics for all units in the faction’s base roster. The new cosmetics will be automatically granted to anyone who purchased the corresponding set before update 2.3.0. These sets include:
Board Room (US Forces)
Earth Red (US Forces)
Sea Blue (US Forces)
Charcoal (Wehrmacht)
Dark Brown (Wehrmacht)
Mud Brown (British Forces)
Nature’s Vanguard (British Forces)
Woodland Slate (British Forces)
Basalt Grey (Deutsches Afrikakorps)
Light Grey (Deutsches Afrikakorps)
As previously noted, the exceptions to this will include the Night Fighters set and the Devil’s Brigade set.

As the changes we are implementing to the store are quite profound, we want to make sure we do right by players who may have already owned some, but not all, the unit cosmetics in a new Ultimate Set. Therefore, with this update any player who previously owned at least one unit cosmetic for a given set will now be granted the full Ultimate Set.
The exceptions to this will include the Night Fighters set and the Devil’s Brigade set.

We previously announced changes to the Hammer & Shield Expansion Pack which you can read about here. For anyone that does not currently own the US Forces Advanced Infantry Battlegroup and the Wehrmacht Italian Coastal Defense Battlegroup, you will be able to purchase them on the Steam Store with the new Hammer & Shield Battlegroup Pack, releasing on April 14th, 2026. These Battlegroups will be delisted from the in-game store today.

For players that may have previously unlocked one, but not both Battlegroups via the in-game store, you will automatically be granted the other Battlegroup on March 31st. We want to ensure that anyone that was saving up or waiting to complete the set doesn’t get left out. So, for example, if you already unlocked or owned the Italian Coastal Defense Battlegroup, but not the Advanced Infantry Battlegroup, you will be granted the latter.

One of the points of feedback we see frequently from players is that they want more item types to spend their Merit and War Bonds on. With the Topaz Rhino update, we will be introducing new Resource Point cosmetics, starting with our new Ultimate Sets:
Sand & Sky (US Forces)
Hinterhalt Elite (Wehrmacht)
Desert Defenders (British Forces)
Stalkers (Deutsches Afrikakorps)
In the future, we hope to add additional cosmetic items and Profile customization options, such as titles, badges, or banners, to the in-game store.

Our goal with these changes is to better package cosmetics and Battlegroups and to make the in-game store experience as streamlined as possible. These changes are also laying the groundwork for future content and DLC so that we can continue improving upon the Company of Heroes 3 experience.
We’re excited to reveal more of the changes coming in the Topaz Rhino update on March 31st, and we can’t wait to share more about future Battlegroups, improvements, and content in the months ahead.
The Company of Heroes Team
Q: If I own part of a cosmetic set, do I need to do anything, or upgrade, or purchase additional items to complete it?
A: No! After March 31st, all Ultimate Sets will include all cosmetic items for that themed faction set. If you own part of it already, you will be granted the remaining items to complete the set.
Q: Will you be releasing any individual unit cosmetics in the future?

A: This is very unlikely. Our goal is to primarily release unit cosmetics as complete Ultimate Sets to cover an entire faction’s base roster. Profile Customizations, Resource Points, Victory Points, and/or Buildings will be the only single purchasable items in the store in the future. Cosmetics for playable/controllable units will be kept to Ultimate Sets.
Q: If I already owned the Hammer & Shield Expansion Pack or the Company of Heroes 3: Premium Edition, will I lose access to any items?
A: No – all previously claimed items will still be tied to your account.
Q: Once the Hammer & Shield Battlegroup Pack is released on April 14th, 2026, if I have a problem purchasing it on the Steam Store or want a refund, who should I contact?
A: You should reach out to Steam Support here.

Giddy up, Explorers 🤠 Core Keeper’s 1.3 Update, Riders of the Underground, is coming on September 21st! We’re so excited to be bringing you an update with a whole host of new features and content that you’ll be able to enjoy across all stages of your underground adventure. From all-new ways to traverse the underground on rideable mounts, to a new sub-biome and improvements to the Mage & Summoner play styles, we’re ready to share some (but not all!) of what you’ve got to look forward to.

You asked for it, and we delivered! Introducing rideable mounts, a new and adorable way to travel in Core Keeper. From 1.3, every single type of cattle in the game will now be rideable thanks to the introduction of the Saddle. All you have to do is approach your desired mount with the Saddle in hand, place it on the cattle, and then ride off into the sunset (that last part is optional). This exciting new feature also comes with its very own UI where you can change your mount’s name and adjust its behaviour to decide whether it stays in place, roams freely, or follows you around when you’re not riding it. Of course, you can also remove the Saddle entirely and return your mount to its former “cattle” status!

In the darker, more humid corners of the Forgotten Ruins, a new sub-biome emerges. Welcome to the Moss sub-biome – a collection of, surprisingly lush, patches of greenery that can be found dotted all over these stoney ruins. With a cozy atmosphere and no natural predators, the Moss sub-biome provides a respite from the destructive Caveling activity in the Forgotten Ruins…though that isn’t to say the odd Caveling doesn’t wander in from time to time.

This peaceful sub-biome also brings with it a new breed of cattle in the form of the raptor-like Orex! Orexes might have all the hallmarks of a vicious predator (front-facing eyes, sharp teeth, powerful jaws), but their diet is entirely critter based and they are typically quite placid in nature.

We’ve been listening to your feedback on Core Keeper’s magic system and have made some adjustments to improve the Mage & Summoner play styles. This includes rebalancing and restructuring some of the talents in the Magic and Summoning skill trees, along with the addition of a new weapon type for Summoners and new staff weapons for Mages. The way summons are spawned and persist has also been improved, but we’ll let you experiment with this on your own. We can’t wait to hear your feedback once you’ve tried it out! ✨

The eagle-eyed among you might have spotted the Hookshot being teased in one or two of our posts on social media recently. This new off-hand item enables Explorers to cross the many pits that run through the underground; provided it has something to hook onto, of course. While the Hookshot might not entirely remove the need for bridges, it's a great (and speedy!) way to jump over small chasms, allowing you to explore further afield and look incredibly cool while doing so.

We’re bringing not one, not two, but THREE new pets to 1.3! The Hoppet is a friend from the sea who keeps enemies at bay with ranged attacks that have the potential to apply the slippery effect. Azeos Jr is a friend from the skies who fires projectile shards and has the ability to stun your enemies. There’s more to discover about these cute creatures, including their various colour combinations, but we’ll leave that up to you!
“Wait, you’ve only told us about two of the new pets…” we hear you say! Well, we’re keeping the third a surprise for now. All we can say is that we hope you love this little pal as much as we do! 😉

We’re adding 10 new armour pieces, 15 new rings, 15 new necklaces, new pouches, new enemies, and new weapons! We’re giving you the option to customise your cursor and crosshair indicators and making paintbrush areas re-sizeable, along with a bunch of balancing adjustments in an effort to improve the overall gameplay experience.

In our quest to make travel and transport more enjoyable, boats, mine carts, and go-karts will now go to your inventory if you die while riding them, and we’ve made some improvements to the go-kart handbrake, turning, and inertia for smoother rides. Players can also expect a bunch of quality-of-life improvements including a new key bind to cycle through loadouts and the ability to compare gear…we know how much you love to optimize your builds!

As always, this is just the tip of the iceberg, and you’ll be able to see exactly what’s been added in our patch notes when the update launches! For the time being, we want to thank you for your support while we’ve worked on 1.3 and to remind you that this is just the first stop on the Road to the Maw. We’re looking forward to hearing your feedback and can’t wait to bring you even more!

releases.displayName: Core Keeper’s Bags & Blasts Update Is Coming March 10th!

items.text: Explorers, get ready to dig into some brand new Core Keeper content! We’re very happy to announce that Core Keeper: Bags & Blasts, the first big update for the game since launch, will be available on all platforms on March 10th 2025. This is a major new content update that will be available to download to all Core Keeper players, so get ready to uncover lots of exciting new additions throughout the game, whether you’re just starting your underground adventure or you’re well on your way to powering up the Core.

Move over Ra-Akar, there’s a new insect in the desert, and she makes for a royal challenge! Introducing Nimruza, Queen of the Burrowed Sands – a super cicada emanating a dark and malevolent energy. Nimruza can be found within The Desert of Beginnings and brings an exciting new boss fight to Core Keeper. If you’ve been keeping up with our Notes From the Underground series, you’ll have spotted references to Nimruza and her brood’s complicated history with the Cavelings. Can you do what they could not and defeat this royal family once and for all?

Picture this: you’ve been wandering The Desert of Beginnings for what feels like forever when, suddenly, you come across what looks like a veritable paradise. Fear not, Explorer, this is no mirage, it’s our new Oasis Sub-Biome! This warm and welcoming desert sanctuary features all-new flora, in the form of Aloe plants and Water Reeds, as well as a new species of cattle that produces a handy (albeit, smelly) resource!

There are a lot of treasures and trinkets to find in Core Keeper, but an abundance of items can often mean a full inventory, and this is something we’ve been keen to revisit for our first major update. There have been plenty of community suggestions and requests for an updated inventory management system, and we’ve thought long and hard about how best to implement this. The solution? Pouches! These handy add-ons allow you to carry items like ores, seeds, fish, and valuables with you in separate, dedicated spaces, providing new ways to organise your items without sacrificing valuable inventory space.

There’s no prizes for guessing what’s coming based on the “Blasts” portion of the update title, but give yourself a pat on the back anyway if you correctly guessed that we’ll be adding more bombs to the game! We’ve had lots of fun coming up with unique ways for each of our new bombs to interact with the world, but the fun doesn’t stop there. We’re also bringing a whole new set of explosives to the game in the form of throwable grenades, each with their own individual effects. Oh, and you can expect a brand-new “Explosives” skill tree to master alongside these new additions.

It wouldn’t be a major content update without a whole host of new equipment. We’ve added all sorts of new and exciting loot for you to find, including tools, armour sets, weapons, off-hand items, and workbenches. From Garden Trowels, to help with seed placement, all the way to the scientific Laboratory Table, there’s plenty to sink your teeth into.

That’s right, the new boss, sub-biome, pouches, explosives, and equipment are just the tip of the iceberg! Bags & Blasts is a major update, which means it’s just bursting with new additions. From even more inventory management features (quick-stack to nearby chests, anyone?) all the way to new decorations, enemies, and more. You’ll find new content across the entirety of the game, with plenty of community requested features – including more content for the Mage & Summoner classes – and lots of fun surprises along the way.

We can’t wait to hear what you think of the Bags & Blasts Update when it launches on March 10th. In the meantime, be sure to keep an eye out for more insights and info about the new update over on the official Core Keeper X, BlueSky, and Discord accounts!
